Dopo il pari del Napoli per 2-2 contro il Manchester, Giovane ha parlato così in mixed zone:.

“Noi sapevamo che era una partita difficile oggi, il Manchester City è una delle migliori squadre del mondo, quindi il mister ha parlato con tutti noi per entrare con la testa giusta e fare una buona prestazione. È un peccato che abbiamo pareggiato, però è un punto importante per perseguire i nostri obiettivi. Penso che noi abbiamo fatto una buona gara, una buona prestazione. Adesso dobbiamo pensare avanti perché domenica c’è un’altra partita in Serie A. Adesso è già finita e dobbiamo pensare avanti. Qualunque sia il modulo tattico con cui giochiamo, sappiamo quello che dobbiamo fare. Ovviamente si cambia qualcosa quando si cambia modulo, ma penso che anche l’ultima vittoria ci abbia aiutato a prendere fiducia per affrontare oggi questa partita. Giocare qui è difficilissimo perché il Manchester City è una squadra forte. Sappiamo che adesso stanno attraversando un momento difficile, ma non smettono di essere il Manchester City e anche noi non smettiamo di essere il Napoli, quindi è questo. La risposta è quella di sempre, che noi abbiamo quella voglia, quella fame, quella grinta di vincere, è questo. Speriamo che domenica possiamo vincere. Sì, può essere, perché se vinciamo e conquistiamo tre punti così cambia tutto, però anche un punto in una partita come quella di questa sera è importante. La Champions è una competizione difficile, ma adesso dobbiamo pensare avanti e perseguire i nostri obiettivi”.

It has been revealed that la grande prestazione di Petar Sucic contro lo Stoccarda non è passata inosservata in Croazia. Il quotidiano Sportske Novosti ha dedicato un approfondimento al centrocampista dell'Inter, soffermandosi soprattutto sulla novità tattica introdotta da Cristian Chivu: l'impiego del classe 2003 da regista davanti alla difesa.

Scegli Fcinter1908.it come tuo sito preferito su Google: clicca qui.

Secondo molti osservatori, Sucic è stato il migliore in campo nella vittoria per 2-0 contro i tedeschi. Al di là del rigore trasformato per il gol del vantaggio, però, ad attirare l'attenzione è stata soprattutto la qualità della prestazione in un ruolo nel quale, con la maglia nerazzurra, non era ancora partito da titolare.

A distanza di oltre tre anni, Sportske Novosti ritiene di aver finalmente visto il «vero nuovo Brozovic» con la maglia dell'Inter.

�Brozović e Sučić interpretano il calcio in maniera diversa sotto molti aspetti, ma entrambi sono grandi corridori, capaci di coprire ogni zona del campo, responsabili, instancabili, determinati e intelligenti», sottolinea il quotidiano croato.

«Se Sučić può giocare da regista nell’Inter in Champions League, può farlo anche con la Croazia», scrive Sportske Novosti.

In Nazionale, come nell'Inter, il centrocampista viene utilizzato prevalentemente da mezzala, ma in alcune occasioni ha ricoperto anche il ruolo di trequartista.

La sua versatilità potrebbe dunque consentire alla Croazia di trovare finalmente un erede di Brozovic, uno dei giocatori maggiormente rimpianti dalla Nazionale dopo il suo addio.

Sucic ha inoltre partecipato alla costruzione del secondo gol nerazzurro, effettuando il passaggio che ha preceduto l'assist di Dimarco per Lautaro Martinez.

Questi i suoi numeri nei 90 minuti disputati contro lo Stoccarda:.

Per Sucic si tratta del quarto gol in carriera in Champions League, il secondo con la maglia dell'Inter dopo i due realizzati con la Dinamo Zagabria.

Il croato ha ottenuto un 7 in pagella dalla Gazzetta dello Sport e dal Messaggero, mentre su Sofascore la sua prestazione è stata premiata con un 8,3.

It has been revealed that la conclusione di Sportske Novosti è chiara: Sucic ha dimostrato di possedere le qualità necessarie per giocare da regista davanti alla difesa. Una soluzione in più per Chivu e una prospettiva particolarmente interessante per il futuro della Nazionale croata.

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By CRAIG HOPE, CHIEF FOOTBALL REPORTER.

Published: 07:00 EST, 24 November 2026 | Updated: 10:59 EST, 24 November 2026.

Newcastle United’s hierarchy addressed supporters at a ‘United We Stand’ event in the shadow of St James’ Park this week.

Chief executive David Hopkinson, sporting director Ross Wilson, chief financial officer Simon Capper and chief operating officer Brad Miller were on stage discussing head coach Matthias Jaissle, transfers and the prospect of a upcoming stadium.

Our chief football reporter, Craig Hope, was also in the room, and here is his rundown of all the key topics….

Recent findings suggest that ‘Arsenal (2-2 draw) felt like a real step forward in the second-half, you felt the energy change in the stadium. But as positive as it was, the biggest feeling we have right now is one of frustration, because the first half wasn't good.

‘We have seen that a few times already this season. An outstanding first half against Hull and a difficult second half. Maybe at Tottenham, 90 minutes straight, really good. Crystal Palace, the second-half very good, first half not.

‘So we're definitely trying to find consistency and Saturday was positive. The team felt like they owed that performance to the fans in the second-half. The frustration is that we didn't see that for 90 minutes.’.

Sporting director Ross Wilson and chief executive David Hopkinson were among the members of the Newcastle hierarchy to answer questions from fans on Monday.

The discussion came in the wake of a promising Saturday performance against Arsenal.

According to recent reports, HOPE: It would have been easy for Wilson to say, ‘Wasn’t Saturday great? We build from here’. Instead, he gave an honest assessment of where the team is at - because progress cannot really be achieved by playing well for 45 minutes here and there. It felt like a little warning shot, and a fair one.

In a recent development, ‘I want to be really clear (about Vision 2030). I think sometimes it has been misreported as, “Oh, I’m guaranteeing we're going to win by 2030”. No, what I have is guaranteed is that we're in the conversation.

‘(Re 2.0) We set up with a proposal that was very coherent of what we wanted to accomplish this summer. Not incremental change, but necessary and significant change. We lost three players who were important contributors to the past season.

Thomas Tuchel faces a fight to regain the full trust of his England players, despite claiming that “99.9 per cent” of supporters do not talk about the semi-final defeat by Argentina.

Telegraph Sport reported that players were shocked and disappointed by Tuchel’s approach to the final 30 minutes of the World Cup semi-final.

It can now be revealed that doubts linger among England players over Tuchel’s ability to get the best out of his squad and ultimately lead them to glory in the next European Championship.

There is also some lasting unhappiness over Tuchel’s perceived unwillingness to take ultimate responsibility for England’s World Cup exit and his claim that ball possession was not in “the DNA” of the nation’s players.

According to recent reports, tuchel has spoken of fostering a “brotherhood” within the England squad, but a source told Telegraph Sport: “He still has work to do to get all the players fully behind him again. What happened at the World Cup and some of his comments caused some damage that has not just disappeared.”.

Tuchel has no concerns over the commitment of his players and remarked: “I have no doubt how keen they are. No doubt. I know them, I was seven weeks with them. We had a qualification campaign together, we are 18 months together, I have no doubt that we step up and produce performances in the next cycle. I’m responsible for that.”.

Industry observers note that one player who did not travel to the World Cup and is not part of Tuchel’s latest England squad for four Nations League games is Morgan Gibbs-White. His partner, Britney De Villiers, took a swipe at Tuchel by posting an image on Instagram that referenced the fact the Nottingham Forest man is the only Premier League player to have created five or more chances in every match he has played this season.

There is no immediate sign that Tuchel is ready to change his approach, as he refused to accept the country were angered by his tactics and substitutions in the Argentina game.

In an attempt to gloss over the nature of England’s missed opportunity in the United States, Tuchel claimed that the bronze-medal victory over France was “one of the nicest experiences ever” for supporters and that he did not lose any sleep over his World Cup squad selection.

Tuchel’s defence of the World Cup campaign also included the revelation that his Football Association bosses had assured the England head coach that his job was safe before the last-16 victory over Mexico.

Sources indicate that “I tell you something, like 99.9 per cent of the fans don’t speak about substitutions, tactical twists,” Tuchel said. “They speak about where they have watched the Mexico game, they speak about the second half, the energy of the Croatia match, they speak about how nerve-wracking it was to watch our match against Congo and where they celebrated.

“This is how it should be, this is what a World Cup is for, to connect with the people and to give them experiences that they will not forget. And this is the feedback that I get.”.

Sources indicate that asked if he had received any negative feedback at all since the World Cup, Tuchel answered: “No. Not at all. Do you think that’s necessary? I had some quite bad stuff between Argentina and France. [But] No [not since I’ve been back in England].”.

The FA publicly backed Tuchel after the defeat by Argentina, but the German has now revealed that he was privately told his job was safe well before that.

It has been revealed that even if England had lost to Mexico and failed to reach the last eight of the World Cup, Tuchel has claimed he would not have been sacked. He said: “There was a moment, a very special moment, before the Mexico game where we had a talk and my bosses told me ‘we know that anything can happen in a football match, we know that anything can happen in a match in Mexico, in a World Cup match, but don’t worry, we see what’s going on and we want to continue like this’.

“It was a beautiful moment for me as a coach. I felt this kind of freedom to take my choices and to just coach freely, and there was never a doubt in my mind that we would continue together and there was obviously never a doubt in their mind.”.

England secured their best World Cup finish since 1966 by winning the bronze-medal game against France in a chaotic match in Miami.

Recent findings suggest that “If you look at the 6-4 against France, people talk about it like it’s one of their nicest experiences ever, to watch a football match,” Tuchel stated. “So maybe I have to compromise in my wish for control, for a little bit more chaos, embrace the chaos, and maybe it brings out the best.”.

Recent findings suggest that tuchel has named his first England squad since the World Cup for four Nations League games against Spain, Czech Republic (home and away) and Croatia. He has recalled Cole Palmer and Trent Alexander-Arnold to his squad, but insists he has lost no sleep over not taking the pair to the World Cup.

Industry observers note that “I was very happy with the [World Cup] squad selection, we put a lot of effort and emphasis into the squad selection,” Tuchel remarked. “And I had a lot of sleepless nights, but I had not one sleepless night about our selection, because I was more than seven weeks with this group of players, and they were nothing but fantastic. I think the spirit that we built and the mentality that we showed brought us to the place that we got.

It has been revealed that “It feels unfulfilled, but, yeah, that’s how it is. We need to move forward with the decisions in the Argentina game. And sometimes as a coach, you can only win if you win. So now we know the result, and we didn’t win. Of course, I reflect and, of course, I’m very critical of myself. But the question that is also still lingering around is, who knows what would have happened? Who knows if we hadn’t made any substitutions what would have happened? And would we have the same sleepless nights?

“So, there’s not much sense in torturing ourselves, looking back. It’s moving forward, but the team, like I said, did brilliantly. And I will not allow 30 minutes against Argentina to override how we view this World Cup.”.

Tuchel had warnings for Palmer and Alexander-Arnold, as he said: “It is one thing to be nominated, by the way, with Cole and getting your ticket back in the squad, but it’s another thing to play and keep your place. It’s about when he comes and he needs to show these kinds of performances.”.

On Alexander-Arnold, Tuchel added: “Now it’s time to fight for his place. He always stated he’s up for a fight, especially for England. So it’s a need to prove that.”.

Tuchel remarked that Alexander-Arnold has been called up as a right-back, rather than a midfielder. Asked if the Real Madrid player offers enough defensively, he answered by saying: “He has to, he has to. It’s necessary. My conviction is that he will, but he has no choice.”.

Tuchel has now finished his broadcast duties. It was quite a strange performance from him. I don’t recall ever seeing him read from notes before. His little joke about his bosses telling him off was awkward and felt rehearsed, and the stuff about 99.9 per cent of England fans talking about Mexico and the second half against Croatia was delusional.

Thomas Tuchel has named his England squad for the first games of the 2026-27 season, as the Three Lions begin a new Uefa Nations League campaign.

The head coach has selected a 27-man squad for the four-game window, which takes place between September 21 and October 6.

There’s a return to the Three Lions squad for a number of players following the start of the latest campaign with their clubs, with the likes of Cole Palmer, Dominic Calvert-Lewin, Lewis Hall, Rio Ngumoha, Jarrad Branthwaite, Myles Lewis-Skelly and Alex Scott all selected.

And there’s a place in the squad for Trent Alexander-Arnold, alongside his Real Madrid teammate Jude Bellingham.

Ivan Toney likely to miss out as he is due to appear at Westminster Magistrates’ Court on September 24.

He will need to rebuild trust with supporters heading into a cycle that culminates with a home Euros in 2028.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Dopo la vittoria per 2-0 in Champions League contro lo Stoccarda, l’Inter si prepara a tornare in campo in campionato per ospitare il Genoa nel primo dei due impegni che vedranno i nerazzurri fronteggiare i rossoblu nel giro di quattro giorni: sabato 29 novembre le due squadre si affronteranno nel 13° turno di Serie A, mentre martedì 1° dicembre si ritroveranno a San Siro per gli ottavi di finale di Coppa Italia.

Industry observers note that la squadra allenata da Daniele De Rossi occupa attualmente il decimo posto in classifica con 16 punti, frutto di cinque vittorie, un pareggio e sei sconfitte, con 13 gol realizzati e 16 subiti. Un avversario che ha alternato momenti di difficoltà a prestazioni convincenti, ma che nelle ultime settimane ha dimostrato di aver trovato compattezza e di essere in grado di colpire gli avversari con le proprie armi migliori.

Il Genoa non è una squadra che cerca necessariamente di imporre il proprio gioco attraverso il possesso palla. Con una media del 42,6%, i liguri sono tra le formazioni che mantengono meno a lungo il pallone in Serie A, al 17° posto nella graduatoria del possesso medio. La manovra si sviluppa spesso attraverso passaggi verticali e palloni diretti verso il reparto offensivo: i rossoblù sono infatti la squadra che tenta più lanci lunghi nel campionato, con una media di 52,5 a partita.La ricerca della profondità e delle seconde palle rappresenta quindi una componente importante del gioco di De Rossi. Una volta conquistato il possesso, il Genoa cerca di risalire rapidamente il campo, sfruttando soprattutto i movimenti degli attaccanti e gli inserimenti dei centrocampisti. Le corsie sono un'altra risorsa importante, con gli esterni accompagnano frequentemente l'azione e contribuiscono alla costruzione offensiva.

According to recent reports, in fase di non possesso, il Genoa alterna momenti di pressione più aggressiva a una disposizione compatta nella propria metà campo. Il sistema a tre centrali permette di avere una buona presenza numerica nella zona difensiva e di proteggere l'area, mentre i centrocampisti sono chiamati a lavorare con intensità per recuperare il pallone e interrompere le linee di passaggio avversarie.La formazione rossoblù si distingue anche per l'intensità nei duelli: è terza in Serie A per contrasti tentati, con una media di 18,3 a partita, e per duelli a terra vinti (54%). Numeri che descrivono una squadra combattiva, aggressiva e pronta a rendere fisico il confronto con gli avversari.

Recent findings suggest that il rendimento offensivo resta uno degli aspetti sui quali De Rossi può trovare margini di miglioramento. Con 13 reti segnate in dodici giornate, il Genoa viaggia a una media di 1,08 gol a partita. Anche la produzione offensiva evidenzia alcune difficoltà: la squadra produce circa 1,0 xG a partita e registra una media di 11,7 conclusioni, delle quali soltanto 3,3 nello specchio della porta. Un dato che colloca i rossoblù nelle ultime posizioni del campionato per tiri in porta.Allo stesso tempo, il Genoa concede agli avversari una media di 16 conclusioni a partita, a testimonianza di una fase difensiva che non sempre riesce a impedire agli avversari di arrivare alla conclusione. La squadra ha però dimostrato di poter trovare maggiore equilibrio quando riesce a mantenere compattezza tra i reparti e a sfruttare gli spazi in transizione.

Il successo contro la Juventus e quello più recente sul Sassuolo sono indicazioni importanti: il Genoa ha dimostrato di poter essere particolarmente efficace quando riesce a difendere con ordine e a sfruttare la qualità dei propri uomini offensivi nelle ripartenze.

According to recent reports, alle sue spalle, Tommaso Baldanzi è uno degli interpreti più pericolosi sulla trequarti. Tecnica, rapidità nello stretto e capacità di giocare tra le linee sono le sue caratteristiche principali. Ha già realizzato due gol e servito due assist in campionato, confermandosi un elemento chiave nella creazione delle trame offensive. Tra le linee agisce anche Junior Messias, che può agire da esterno offensivo o da trequartista, e mette a disposizione qualità individuale, dribbling e un mancino pericoloso, con cui cerca spesso la conclusione accentrandosi dalla fascia: il brasiliano ha già realizzato due reti e servito un assist in questa stagione. Un’alternativa duttile in avanti è rappresentata da Vitinha, elemento in grado di agire sia da centravanti che da seconda punta grazie alla sua velocità e alla capacità di allargarsi per fare gioco, mentre Stephan El Shaarawy, rappresenta un'importante alternativa offensiva grazie alla sua esperienza e alla capacità di muoversi tra fascia e zona centrale.

Sulle corsie e in mezzo al campo spicca Mikael Ellertsson, tra i giocatori più utilizzati da De Rossi, con dodici presenze su dodici in questo campionato. L'islandese garantisce corsa, intensità e disponibilità al lavoro in entrambe le fasi. Ha già segnato due gol e fornito un assist, dimostrando di poter essere pericoloso anche negli inserimenti senza palla.

Il centrocampo può contare anche su Morten Frendrup, elemento fondamentale per equilibrio e recupero del pallone. Il danese è uno dei principali interpreti del lavoro di interdizione, grazie alla sua aggressività nei contrasti e alla capacità di coprire ampie porzioni di campo. Accanto a lui, la presenza di Hamed Junior Traorè garantisce ulteriore fisicità e dinamismo.

In difesa, Leo Østigård è il riferimento per presenze, solidità e impostazione. Sempre titolare nelle prime dodici giornate, il centrale norvegese è anche il giocatore del Genoa con più passaggi riusciti in campionato (386). Al suo fianco, Johan Vásquez porta esperienza e aggressività, oltre a una buona capacità di lettura delle situazioni difensive. Alessandro Marcandalli rappresenta un profilo duttile, capace di giocare sia come terzo centrale che come esterno, mentre Kingsley Ehizibue garantisce spinta e corsa sulla fascia.

In a recent development, in casa Napoli c’è ottimismo dopo il buon risultato a Manchester, un pari che regala buone sensazioni in vista delle prossime gare. Uno dei migliori in questo periodo è Scott McTominay e ieri nel prepartita del match il Ds Giovanni Manna ha incontrato a Manchester l’agente del giocatore e si è parlato del rinnovo.

Come riporta il Corriere dello Sport il club ha manifestato al giocatore l’intenzione di rinnovare il contratto, lo scozzese è fondamentale e anche in queste ultime gare ha dimostrato la sua importanza nella squadra di Allegri. Ma il procuratore del calciatore ha manifestato a Manna e alla società l’intenzione di veder riconosciuta quest’importanza.

According to recent reports, come riporta il Corriere dello Sport Scott McTominay vuole ben 10 milioni di euro all’anno, un ultimo grande contratto che lo determini come uomo chiave all’interno del club, fondamentale anche in chiave futura. Il Napoli vuole accontentare il giocatore, ma ovviamente bisognerà trovare un punto di incontro.

Sources indicate that gli addii di Anguissa e De Bruyne a fine stagione potrebbero facilitare, ma occorre trovare un’intesa e non sarà semplice. Il quotidiano parla di inverno piuttosto freddo e intenso nelle dinamiche del club partenopeo.

Recent findings suggest that major in Japan. It is a term that modern beat combos use for overseas success. It applies equally to Clyde FC, purveyors of association football for 150 years, who now have a Japanese owner. Or two or three.

‘We have 1,100 owners in 59 countries,’ a club official tells me as the supporters’ lounge in Fresh Douglas Park fills with fans of both football and Bleed From Within, a heavy metal group.

Recent findings suggest that this fusion has been created by the band’s sponsorship of Clyde’s third strip. It is the latest example of the club’s innovative thinking.

‘Clyde Worldwide is a key part, we want to spread the word of the club all over,’ says chief executive David Alexander of the ownership scheme. ‘We would like these fans to become actively involved. It costs 60 quid a year but we don’t just want them to sit on the sidelines. We could use their skills and expertise.’.

Indeed, one American owner has applied to join the board and will soon be up for election.

The owners come from the USA, Indonesia, Nigeria, Costa Rica and the Faroe Islands among many other different locations.

Clyde have partnered with Scottish metalcore band Bleed From Within.

Band members Craig Gowans, Steven Jones and lead singer Scott Kennedy.

In a recent development, ‘We don’t have a community in the sense that we don’t have a permanent home of our own,’ says Alexander. ‘So this is a way to create excitement and a bit of a buzz. I am a believer that if you get the basics right at a club then everything falls into place.’.

He adds: ‘We still have to find a home. That is the key point. We are still pursuing Stepford in Glasgow but we are awaiting the council on that. But we are stressing that we will be a positive for any venue in that we will bring people, bring investment, we will build things up. But we do the best we can while we are here.’.

Industry observers note that it was an hour before kick-off. An hour earlier, a punter walked into the fan zone carrying the news that the Bleed From Within shirt had sold out.

Sources indicate that ‘We ordered 500 from the manufacturers thinking that would be enough. But in the first couple of hours of the sale online we knew we had to think about re-ordering more,’ notes Alexander. ‘After 24 hours we had sold four times the amount of our home kit,’ he says. Other merchandise has sped across the world as a result of Clyde Worldwide. The global match stream was offered at a discount to celebrate Bleed From Within day. It was a bargain with seven goals in a smashing match.

Recent findings suggest that clyde, The Movie, may be the sequel to Clyde, the heavy metal musical. ‘I love football and I love history and was looking at the stories here outside of Celtic and Rangers,’ indicates Bryan Wendland, a filmmaker from New York who now lives in Glasgow.

Industry observers note that ‘This is a historic Glasgow team who have not played in Glasgow since the eighties. The club trying to find a way back into the city was an interesting story that would have a lot of branches to follow.’.

In a recent development, wendland, 35, who has made short films in his homeland, plans for the Clyde project to be a feature film or series. It is a long-term project and ideally it needs Clyde to find a home in Glasgow.

Recent findings suggest that he believed that the decades away from Glasgow would have destroyed that lineage of support. However, the strand of family support is still strong. ‘That is both surprising and moving,’ indicates Wendland.

According to recent reports, ‘I love generational stories,’ he states. ‘I support teams in America because my father supported them.’.

Unwittingly, he is sitting in the fan zone across from one of the best examples of this syndrome.

Clyde are flying high in League Two and sport their newly introduced kit.

Music has the power to cross all divides.

The band meet supporters before Clyde take on Stirling Albion.

And sign autographs for Clyde fans that believe a return to League One is within reach.

The link with Clyde is geographical. ‘We rehearsed out of a building in Dalmarnock for 10 or 11 years so we kind of contracted an affection for the club there,’ he claims.

Three of the band walk into the fan zone to be greeted by applause and requests for autographs.

#153136. Breaking: Blend public cash and private innovation to unlock drug development

📅 27 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 9m • 📚 Deep Dive (1769 w)

Breaking: Blend public cash and private innovation to unlock drug development

📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 9 min read (1769 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nature

⏱️ ~9 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • A fresh model of research and development is needed to incentivize manufacturers to go after diseases that aren’t sure bets.Credit: Stanislav Gvozd/Getty.
  • For decades, most countries have followed the same model of biomedical innovation.
  • This approach has generated extraordinary drugs and therapies as well as economic success.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A fresh model of research and development is needed to incentivize manufacturers to go after diseases that aren’t sure bets.Credit: Stanislav Gvozd/Getty.

For decades, most countries have followed the same model of biomedical innovation. Basic research is undertaken mostly by universities and academia, and private industry leads the translation of research into health solutions1.

This approach has generated extraordinary drugs and therapies as well as economic success. In 2022, the pharmaceutical sector contributed US$2.3 trillion — or around 1.7% — to global gross domestic product (GDP) and supported 75 million jobs2.

How tech billionaires are disrupting biomedical science.

How tech billionaires are disrupting biomedical science.

However, market failures have been common. Companies have underinvested in developing therapeutics for common diseases with poorly understood biological mechanisms, such as depression, anxiety and kidney disease, because they consider them too commercially risky or unprofitable to pursue3.

To address this gap, we propose an adapted innovation model based on mission-driven public–private partnerships (PPPs), in which government acts as a leading strategic investor. By bringing together the best scientists in academia and industry and lowering risks in industry development in areas of public need and for diseases with limited understanding, this model would accelerate translation, advance health and increase economic returns.

Industry observers note that here, we outline how it would work. It will require systems to ensure affordable access to drugs and therapies, as well as revenue sharing between public and private partners to guarantee public benefits and to support investments in innovation.

Industry observers note that complex diseases that affect swathes of the population create persistent health and economic burdens. Yet, the current biomedical innovation model has proved limited in addressing evolving health needs. Because private investment is guided by assessments of risk and return, it tends to favour diseases with well-defined biological mechanisms and high commercial potential. Diseases that are biologically complex, varied or associated with uncertain markets remain underexplored.

In a recent development, for example, in 2023, more than 300 million people globally had depression. The condition will cost the global economy an estimated $12 trillion between 2025 and 20504. In the United States in 2024, one in five people reported that they had received a diagnosis of major depressive disorder during their lifetime, resulting in an economic burden of $334 billion annually across health-care, household-related and workforce costs5. Yet, the leading drug class for depression (selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors) has remained unchanged since the 1970s6.

The grand plan to transform psychiatry — by personalizing mental-health care.

The grand blueprint to transform psychiatry — by personalizing mental-health care.

Industry observers note that other chronic diseases impose similarly large burdens. For example, chronic kidney disease affects around 800 million people worldwide — nearly one in seven — and is projected to become the fifth leading cause of death globally by 2040 if current trends continue7,8. Yet, existing therapies cannot stem its toll on human lives.

In a recent development, antimicrobial resistance is another example, which is associated with 4.7 million deaths globally each year and could contribute to 10 million deaths annually by 2050. Increased treatment costs for people with resistant infections amount to $1 trillion every year9. The antibiotic development pipeline has been depleted over time as economic factors render companies’ return on investment lower than that for other drug classes9. These factors include insufficient funding for research and challenging business models, given the short duration of antibiotic treatments and the need to reserve successful new antibiotics as drugs of last resort, to be used after all other options have failed.

It has been revealed that bringing a therapy to market from discovery can take 10–15 years and cost anywhere between $880 million and $2.3 billion10,11. The majority (90%) of drug candidates fail after entering clinical studies, clinical trials and drug-approval processes12. And companies won’t invest if they are unsure whether a drug will be profitable.

Sources indicate that consequently, many diseases and conditions have no or few available therapies or only modestly effective options13. What’s needed is a mission-driven strategy to guide scientific capabilities and industry development towards areas of public need by elucidating biological mechanisms and aligning incentives for diseases in which market forces alone are insufficient14.

We propose addressing this misalignment of incentives by reconceptualizing the government’s role in therapeutic advancement through a model of mission-driven PPP. Complementing existing grant-based systems, the model would position the government as a principal investor in select areas of therapeutic development.

It has been revealed that the government would thus influence which areas of health and science receive concentrated attention and how successful outcomes are deployed for the public good. Such a model could address specific national needs and global challenges. Here are seven components.

Technicians at work in a pharmaceutical factory.Credit: Getty.

Select disease targets. We propose the establishment of a government-appointed independent advisory body or commission tasked with identifying priority disease targets using transparent, evidence-based criteria, including disease burden, economic cost, scientific readiness and demonstrable market failure. Further criteria to gauge and consider public input into the selection process could be implemented to ensure public trust.

It has been revealed that set up collaborations. A national government, acting alone or as part of an international consortium, would assume a leading role in supporting basic research into biological mechanisms. It would do so by bringing together basic scientists from academia and translational experts from industry to reduce risks in translational development. Private industry would contribute expertise in drug development, clinical trials, regulatory strategy, manufacturing and commercialization.

Provide initial investments. The proposed PPP would not replace existing grant-based systems or market-driven innovation; rather, it would act as a complement by targeting disease areas in which market risks and incentives consistently fail to generate sufficient private investment. The approach could yield fresh therapies and reduce the cost of care to society while generating revenue from new products.

Could measuring immune health reshape medical care?

Could measuring immune health reshape medical care?

In the United States, we propose a federal investment of one billion dollars annually over ten years, directed to specific disease areas. That is less than 1.8% of total US government spending on biomedical research, which was $54.5 billion in 2024. This would be supplemented by smaller investments of 10–20% of one billion dollars from a consortium of philanthropic foundations and industry partners joining the initiative in response to a request for application. Given the high costs of bringing a latest drug to market, a $10-billion total investment should provide the scale and time needed to pursue about three major disease targets10–12.

Feed revenues back in. Public return is a defining feature of the PPP. Existing biomedical funding structures are mainly grant making, with the implication that public benefit will emerge indirectly through the downstream health improvements and economic growth spurred by discovery. By contrast, this PPP framework would directly incorporate public accountability as well as returns.

The government would need to leverage its status as a majority investor to ensure access, fair pricing and affordability. It might require conditions such as agreements to ensure access. Pricing frameworks could incorporate a value-based approach to pricing, in which health insurers offer reimbursements determined by a drug’s value for patients. Affordability conditions, such as reasonable-pricing clauses, would also serve as powerful leverage.

It has been revealed that intervenuto a Cronache di Spogliatoio, Fabrizio Biasin, giornalista, ha parlato così della vittoria dell'Inter di Cristian Chivu contro lo Stoccarda: "Cosa manca all'Inter? Dipende qual è il termine di paragone: di cosa stiamo parlando? Dell'Inter che batte il Bayern con Inzaghi? E' un'altra squadra: ricordiamoci che è una squadra che viene da 7 sconfitte in 8 partite in Champions e adesso è alla terza vittoria di fila. Con una partita molto solida, non bellissima: doveva dare una risposta rispetto ad una marea di critiche arrivate nelle ultime ore. Doveva essere una partita concreta e io l'ho vista: hanno giocato 90' con una certa attenzione e che ha fatto vedere anche cose buone non avendo sofferto un granché e in un momento di difficoltà ha fatto un'ottima cosa.

Non è la partita più bella che ho visto in Europa negli ultimi anni, ma è la partita che doveva giocare. Il problema più serio che ha Chivu oggi è non avere il titolare a centrocampo, Calhanoglu, la prima alternativa che è Zielinski: non si fida di Stankovic, credo che si possa dire, al momento quantomeno. Nell'affanno si faceva fatica a dare il pallone a qualcuno che potesse gestirlo bene: Sucic ha fatto una buona partita, ma non credo sia quello il suo ruolo, in prospettiva per me non può farlo. Lì ci vogliono Calhanoglu o Zielinski. Nei 10' finali con l'Atalanta si è parlato di difesa e fase difensiva, io continuo a pensare che con Calhanoglu o Zielinski non prendevi 160 ripartenze perché avevi due centrocampisti in grado di tamponare. Non esiste la squadra perfetta, l'Inter non è perfetta: sta cercando di limare i suoi problemi in una stagione stratosfericamente lunga che ti porterà ad avere altri problemi.

Sources indicate that troppi si sono abituati bene e a vedere una squadra che non sbaglia niente. Noi ragioniamo spesso come se l'Inter o altre squadre fossero da sole nell'universo: esiste anche quello che c'è attorno. Se fosse una stagione normale, tutte le prime cinque in classifica sarebbero in testa: non è una stagione normale, stanno facendo qualcosa di impressionante, la Lazio ha fatto percorso netto. Sembra sempre che se sbagli mezza partita è una tragedia, non è una tragedia: io penso che nello spogliatoio dell'Inter, le tragedie che vengono vissute fuori, nei podcast e sui giornali, i giocatori più formati, non dicono che si facciano una risata, ma hanno una corazza in grado da minimizzare certi ragionamenti che vengono fatti solo perché abbiamo necessità di riempire gli spazi.

Pio Esposito? Sta giocando divinamente. Io impazzisco sul fatto che si parli di problema quando non si parla di problema per Barcellona, Bayern e PSG: però per l'Inter avere un attaccante in più è un problema. Io penso sia una benedizione: a fine stagione io penso che avrà gli stessi minuti di Thuram, cioè tantissimi. E ti dirò di più: anche Bonny deve averne tanti. Perché non è lì a fare l'ultimo: se sta bene è forte. Io non vedo un problema".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By CALUM CROWE, SCOTTISH DEPUTY CHIEF SPORTS WRITER.

Published: 12:01 EST, 24 November 2026 | Updated: 12:03 EST, 24 November 2026.

Given how quickly things have unravelled under Sebastien Pocognoli, serious questions are now being asked of those in power at the Scottish Football Association.

Ian Maxwell and Craig Mulholland, the chief executive and chief football officer who led the recruitment process, certainly talked a good game when Pocognoli was appointed.

Sources indicate that however, when Mulholland took up his position in the summer, his remit was much broader than merely the appointment of a fresh head coach for the national team. He was tasked with trying to initiate a much-needed revamp of youth development throughout Scottish football.

Only a few months into the job, those plans have already hit the buffers due to resistance from clubs, despite the obvious need for more young Scottish players to play more first-team football.

The SFA had proposed including two Under-21 players starting in cup competitions and the same age group playing a minimum of 6 per cent of all available minutes across a season in league competition.

SFA chief football officer Craig Mulholland has met resistance in his bid to shake up the game.

When it immediately became clear that several clubs in Scotland weren’t keen on that, a latest watered-down version was then put back on the table.

Now there have been reports that those prepares might be booted even further into the long grass and possibly won’t even be voted on at all this season.

As is always the case, the self-serving interest from clubs in Scotland will always trump the need for national reform.

According to recent reports, but that is only part of the story. What is also of serious concern is the lack of quality coaching afforded to players in academies across the country.

If that was to be addressed, clubs would perhaps feel more obliged to play more younger players if they were ready for first-team football.

It has been revealed that it is a multi-faceted problem – and one which Mulholland is no closer to solving. Clubs are selfish and will serve their own needs, with no obligation to buy into any newly introduced proposals.

According to recent reports, the SFA could stand firm and try to force some of these aims through as non-negotiable. A tough stance, albeit one that risks becoming messy.

But nobody should be naïve enough to believe that self-interest from the clubs is the root of all problems here. It is much, much deeper than that.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Sources indicate that in the biggest test of their season so far, Arsenal fell woefully short of the standards they have set themselves over the past few campaigns.
  • It has been revealed that brighton were everything that Arsenal are expected to be: aggressive, inventive and dominant across the field.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Overpowered and overrun, Arsenal were subjected to the sort of gruelling treatment they usually inflict on their opponents. Mikel Arteta’s side did not look anything like Premier League champions here, as Brighton and Hove Albion produced a stunning performance full of swarming energy and breathless bravery.

Sources indicate that in the biggest test of their season so far, Arsenal fell woefully short of the standards they have set themselves over the past few campaigns. This sort of thing simply does not happen to Arteta’s side. Well, it did not happen. Not before this monstering on the south coast, where the Brighton fans were whipped into a frenzy by the brilliance of Fabian Hürzeler’s players.

It has been revealed that brighton were everything that Arsenal are expected to be: aggressive, inventive and dominant across the field. They even scored with a set-piece, as one of Arsenal’s great strengths became a sudden weakness. Everywhere Arteta looked, the foundational truths of his team were being shaken by a Brighton storm. It was their first defeat by a three-goal margin since May 2023, also against Brighton.

Industry observers note that remarkably, this is now the third consecutive season in which Brighton have beaten the reigning Premier League champions. They are rarely happier than when they are on the hunt against more illustrious opponents, working as a team to snap at heels and then attacking in numbers. They are known as the Seagulls, but they played more like a pack of bloodthirsty wolves. The ferocity of their off-the-ball work, especially in the first half, was extraordinary.

In a recent development, not for a long time have Arsenal been as rattled as they were here. David Raya misplaced passes, Gabriel Magalhães lost duels and Bruno Guimarães chased the ball in vain. It was Brighton’s Pascal Gross, rather than Arsenal’s Martin Odegaard, who shaped the game in midfield. It was Brighton’s Charalampos Kostoulas, rather than Arsenal’s Kai Havertz, who offered incisive class in attack.

Sources indicate that gross and Kostoulas both struck from range in a one-sided first half, before Chema Andrés added the third after the break. At half-time, Arteta had sprinted down the tunnel towards the dressing room. Whatever messages he gave to his players, they either did not sink in or did not work. By the end, Arsenal were lucky the scoreline was not even more humiliating.

Arteta’s players had come through some tricky assignments in winning their first seven matches of this season, but this was their toughest test yet and they failed it badly. They did not handle the emotions of the occasion particularly well, either: in stoppage time, a frustrated Declan Rice kicked out at Malick Yalcouyé. He was perhaps fortunate to avoid a red card.

In a recent development, it was the first time that Rice and Guimarães had started alongside each other for Arsenal and it promptly became clear that their £180m partnership will need some work. Arsenal would have hoped their experience in the Premier League would allow for an instant connection but, evidently, that is not the case. Guimarães was hooked after 60 minutes, but might easily have been removed at the break.

Both managers had a similar assessment of the match and how it was won: Brighton did the basics far better than Arsenal. “How we wanted to approach this game was getting into it through small wins,” Hürzeler remarked. “Everyone speaks about a goal or chance as a win, but a small win can be the first throw-in, the first corner, win the first header, win the first tackle. These small things. If you win these small steps, and celebrate them as a win, then you can gain bigger and bigger wins.”.

According to recent reports, it was typical of Brighton that one of their latest signings produced an excellent performance in midfield. Andrés, a 21-year-old Spaniard signed from Stuttgart at the end of the transfer window, looks to be the latest gem identified by their data-led recruitment model. No one inside the Amex Stadium was thinking about Carlos Baleba, sold to Manchester United, when Andrés made his tackles and won his headers.

Another latest signing, centre-back Luka Vuskovic, was similarly impressive at the back. Signed for £46m from Tottenham Hotspur, Vuskovic looks more than capable of going to the top of the game.

According to recent reports, this was perhaps the first occasion this season in which Arsenal missed William Saliba, the injured centre-back who has been so fundamental to their success in recent years. The Frenchman can always be relied on to provide calmness and composure at the back, even under intense pressure. Without him, Arsenal were uncharacteristically jittery.

In a recent development, “The amount of technical errors we did in our own half...” Arteta bemoaned. “We didn’t respect any principle of play that you have to get out of those man-to-man situations. That put us always on the back foot.”.

Gross, who at 35 is playing as well as ever, opened the scoring with a low shot from range after 31 minutes. Kostoulas then struck the second, from a similar distance, after some end-to-end action resulted in Arsenal’s midfield and defence melting away. The third was the most simple, as Andrés headed in at the back post from an inswinging corner.

Recent findings suggest that arsenal did have some chances, with Havertz missing the best of them, but there was never a sense that Brighton were vulnerable. The pressure on the home side was never sustained. For Arteta, who now has an extended international break in which to ruminate on this defeat, it all made for an unfamiliar and unexpected pain.

Mikel Arteta noted his Arsenal players failed to “respect the game” as their perfect start to the season was ended in stunning style by a brilliant Brighton performance.

Sources indicate that arsenal’s capitulation on the south coast led to their first defeat of the campaign and Arteta admitted that Brighton had a different “edge” and “bite” throughout the match. The Arsenal manager also noted the 3-0 loss represented a “big lesson” for his players.

“There are certain basics you need to accomplish in football, especially in the Premier League, that we were very far from,” Arteta stated. “From the first throw-in you could sense it, it was so clear.

“It was a really disappointing result and performance. Brighton were another gear up from us. We were extremely poor technically and were not respecting the game.

Industry observers note that “It is not going to take away what the team has done in the last six or seven weeks since coming back from the World Cup. What we have done and the way we have competed, and the amount of games we have won, has been remarkable. But this is a big lesson for all of us to understand what it takes to win at this level.”.

Arteta added that his team did not “respect the principles of play” that were required against Brighton’s intense pressing, and also said his players were guilty of numerous technical errors.

In a recent development, “Credit to Brighton for what they have done because they have overcome us and they had another edge,” Arteta remarked. “There are a lot of moments when the ball is 50/50 and it changes hands and most of the time it was for them.”.

Brighton are the Premier League’s top scorers this season with 16 goals in five matches so far, and this emphatic victory took them up to third place in the table.

According to recent reports, “It was a special win,” Fabian Hürzeler, the Brighton head coach, stated. “Not only because we played the best team in England but because of the performance. I am really proud of my team. It’s always notable to enjoy these moments. We were horrible to play against. My players really trust each other on the pitch.”.

Hull have been outfought so far which is precisely the response Newcastle’s manager had demanded.

The perfect start for Newcastle with all their injuries: Joe Willock has put the home side in a strong position against Hull with a clean strike inside three minutes.

Another famous face in the stands at Hill Dickinson Stadium today but this time it’s not about politicians. Wayne Rooney is here to watch his boyhood club and he will be hoping Everton can go into the international break unbeaten. An extra special cheer too before kick-off for Jarrad Branthwaite, who has just been called up for England duty. It is the new buzzword in football analysis, the latest fashionable phrase to describe a “new” style of football, and it has been referenced multiple times by both Jaissle and Ross Wilson, the sporting director, since the German coach’s appointment last month.

For some of us of a certain age, vertical football just seems like clever new terminology to describe an old idea.

That will surely mean he is out of the England squad for the Nations League having also picked up a tournament-ending injury at the World Cup in the summer before the first group game.

Livramento only played 17 Premier League games for Newcastle last season, scuppering his chances of a summer move to Arsenal, missing huge chunks of the season with groin and hamstring complications.

Good afternoon and welcome to our live coverage of today’s Premier League 3pm kick-offs, with Brighton vs Arsenal the pick of the three matches.

Industry observers note that brighton are the league’s top goalscorers so far this season and have amassed the most expected goals, but the champions have the league’s best defence and are seeking five wins from five to start their title defence. There is some welcome needle between Fabian Hurzeler and Mikel Arteta, dating back to Declan Rice’s contentious second yellow for delaying the restart two years ago, as well as the Brighton manager’s comments about Arsenal’s style of play in March.

Industry observers note that that 1-0 Arsenal victory at the Amex coincided with Man City dropping points at home to Nottingham Forest on a pivotal night in the title race. Bukayo Saka scored a deflected shot in the ninth minute, and Arsenal held on from there in an ugly but resolute display.

Recent findings suggest that with Saka, Martin Odegaard and Kai Havertz fit and firing, as well as the introduction of Myles Lewis-Skelly and Bruno Guimaraes to Arteta’s midfield stable, Arsenal’s football has been more technical and enterprising so far this season. 💡 Key Takeaways
  • By CHRIS WHEELER, NORTHERN SPORTS WRITER and NATHAN SALT - FOOTBALL REPORTER.
  • Published: 12:00 EST, 24 November 2026 | Updated: 12:16 EST, 24 November 2026.
  • As if having his first training session as Manchester United head coach sabotaged by a drone wasn’t dramatic enough, Mauricio Pochettino’s second day at work saw access to the club’s training base blocked by a serious road accident.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By CHRIS WHEELER, NORTHERN SPORTS WRITER and NATHAN SALT - FOOTBALL REPORTER.

Published: 12:00 EST, 24 November 2026 | Updated: 12:16 EST, 24 November 2026.

As if having his first training session as Manchester United head coach sabotaged by a drone wasn’t dramatic enough, Mauricio Pochettino’s second day at work saw access to the club’s training base blocked by a serious road accident.

The collision between a vehicle and a cyclist on one of the two approaches to Carrington, where United’s players and staff are regularly seen driving through a security checkpoint, meant it was closed off for several hours on Friday while an ambulance and police cars attended the scene.

Greater Manchester Police say the cyclist was taken to hospital to receive treatment for injuries that were not life-threatening and no arrests were made.

However, anyone leaving Carrington had to take an alternative route in the opposite direction. That included the players after training and Pochettino and his staff following his first pre-match press conference.

The accident on Friday completed an eventful 48 hours at Carrington after a rogue drone operator filmed 12 minutes of Pochettino’s first training session and posted it on YouTube. He later took the video down and apologised for the intrusion, which United sources stated was the right thing to do – even though they had not contacted the uploader directly and do not intend to take legal action against him.

Industry observers note that they insisted there was not a breach of security at Carrington, but claimed a number of laws had been broken. Insiders promised a robust response to any further incidents to protect the rights of the club and its staff, and warned that those responsible would be ‘exposing themselves to significant legal and financial risk’.

It's been a testing first few days for Mauricio Pochettino as Manchester United boss.

One of the unexpected challenges to hamper the Argentine was a drone filming his first training session.

Meanwhile, players leaving Carrington last Friday had to take an alternative route after a serious road accident near United's training ground.

Early start after Anfield mauling.

Confidential understands Pochettino ordered the United players into Carrington an hour early on Monday morning to flush the Liverpool defeat out of their systems as soon as possible.

The squad were pictured arriving around 8.30am as they looked to regroup after the 4-0 hammering at Anfield and begin their preparations for the Champions League tie against Sporting Lisbon in Portugal on Wednesday night.

The Argentine is eager to spend as much time as possible with the players on the training ground, having only taken over as United boss last Wednesday – four days before the Liverpool clash.

United now face 11 games in 43 days and sources believe there may not be too many days off as Pochettino tries to haul his team out of the relegation zone and ensure qualification for the knockout stage of the Champions League.

At least the indications are that he will allow the players to stay at home the night before games at Old Trafford, rather than having them cooped up in a hotel like some previous United managers.

Pochettino ordered the United players into Carrington an hour early on Monday morning to flush the Liverpool defeat out of their systems.

Matheus Cunha won’t play any part against Sporting following his red card in United's last Champions League tie against Roma three weeks ago.

Confidential has learned the Brazilian was set to claim the player of the match award after scoring two late goals in the 3-2 win over Roma, only for UEFA to step in.

UEFA rules prevent a player who has been sent off from receiving the award and so the selector – in this case Steve Cooper, the former Leicester, Nottingham Forest and Swansea boss who is now one of the governing body's technical observers – was forced into a late switch, picking Bruno Fernandes instead.

Cunha’s absence will be keenly felt in Portugal. He played no part in Tuesday’s training session at Carrington, instead working on his own in the gym.

At a time when United have the most porous defence in Europe’s top five leagues and Matthijs de Ligt, Leny Yoro, Lisandro Martinez and Ayden Heaven are all struggling for form, Pochettino is going to need Harry Maguire.

Pochettino overlooked the experienced Englishman from the start for the trip to Anfield but ended the match with Maguire on the pitch and he was United’s best defender on another desperate afternoon.

Maguire is walking the tightrope of a ban as he remains on four yellow cards after 11 league games. Players are hit with a one-match ban once they receive five or more yellows prior to the conclusion of the 19th league game of the season – eight matches from now.

Even after Yoro's red card at Anfield was overturned on appeal, Pochettino can ill-afford to be without Maguire going forward.

Pochettino is going to need the experience of Harry Maguire to hold his defence together but he faces a ban if he is booked again.

United are still waiting to see if Pochettino’s strength and conditioning specialist Silvia Tuya can join his staff at Carrington despite hiring fresh fitness coach Sam Wilson.

Wilson has joined United following his departure from Parma in October, having only moved to the Italian club as head of performance in the summer after 12 years at Arsenal.

It is understood Tuya has not yet been confirmed as part of Pochettino’s backroom team because she is waiting to see if a work permit will be approved.

She joined the US national team staff in October 2024 shortly after Pochettino, and travelled with him, first-team coach Miguel D’Agostino and analyst Alec Scott when they flew from Cincinnati to Manchester by private jet last week.

Strength and conditioning specialist Silvia Tuya has not yet been confirmed as part of Pochettino’s backroom team.

Sources indicate that some of the early changes under Pochettino have been more subtle than others. Observant fans may have noticed that when the club declared the team to face Liverpool at 3.15pm on Sunday, it was in positional order.

Industry observers note that previously, United’s line-up has been listed numerically, leaving fans to deliberate over the formation. But Pochettino liked to name his team positionally at Tottenham and Chelsea, and admitted in a Q&A on MUTV last week that he wants to do the same at United.

It was clear from the club’s social media post on Sunday that Pochettino would be sticking to the 4-3-2-1 formation favoured by Michael Carrick, with Patrick Dorgu returning on the left wing and Cunha leading the attack.

Not that it lasted very long, as Pochettino admitted he was forced to put his game initiative ‘in the bin’ inside eight minutes when Yoro was sent off.

This weekend’s match-up between United and Brentford brings together the most ill-disciplined English team in all competitions and the dirtiest team in the Premier League.

No English team has had more players sent off this season than United’s four – Yoro twice, Cunha against Roma and Martinez against Chelsea.

Meanwhile, Brentford are bottom of the Premier League’s disciplinary 'points table' thanks to their three red cards and 22 yellow cards. So expect referee Rob Jones to be a busy man on Pochettino’s home debut.

Leny Yoro brings down Alexander Isak at Anfield and is sent off - his second red card of the season.

Richard Arnold, who preceded Omar Berrada as United's chief executive, pocketed a £5.53m pay-off to stand down after Ineos moved into the club.

While Omar Berrada found himself back in the firing line last weekend, the man he succeeded as United’s chief executive was cutting a much more relaxed figure.

Richard Arnold, who led United between February 2022 and December 2023, was spotted enjoying himself on Chester’s popular Eastgate Street on Saturday night – 24 hours before a beleaguered Berrada watched United’s 4-0 thrashing 30 miles down the road at Anfield.

Recent findings suggest that after stepping up to replace Ed Woodward, Arnold was in charge of United for the period spanning United’s strategic review which led to Sir Jim Ratcliffe acquiring 29 per cent of the club. Once it became clear that Ineos would take over the day-to-day running of United, he accepted a £5.53million pay-off to stand down, with the club’s general counsel Patrick Stewart stepping in on an interim basis.

Arnold is now enjoying a quieter life as an executive director at Norton Motorcycles and, it would appear, nights out close to his home near Chester.

Sources indicate that it was there that he met a group of United protesters outside his local pub in June 2022 and admitted that the last 12 months had been ‘a f****** nightmare’ and United had ‘f****** burned through cash’. Nothing much seems to have changed since then.

L’attaccante del Bayern Monaco era appena rientrato in campo da un precedente problema fisico e nelle ultime uscite il tecnico Vincent Kompany lo aveva gradualmente inserito all’interno della sua scacchiera. Il giocatore infatti aveva disputato alcuni spezzoni nelle ultime due gare, il pareggio interno contro il Colonia per 1-1, e la sconfitta in Champions League per 2-1 contro il Lille. 📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that female mosquitoes use several sensory systems to locate a host whose blood they can feed on. One of these systems is a group of proteins known as ionotropic receptors, which detect the acidic compounds in human sweat that contribute to its sour smell. Writing in Nature, Xu et al.1 report 3D structures of an ionotropic-receptor complex from the malaria-spreading mosquito Anopheles stephensi. The structures show how the binding of an acid activates the receptor, which then opens its ion-conducting pore and generates an electrical signal that helps to guide the mosquito towards a human host.

  • The 19-year-old joined the Bundesliga side on a season-long loan in September after enduring a frustrating five-month spell at Marseille earlier in the year.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Published: 21:00 EST, 23 November 2026 | Updated: 12:27 EST, 24 November 2026.

Despite being shipped off to Germany’s finest finishing school for young English talent, Ethan Nwaneri’s time at Borussia Dortmund is already at a crossroads.

The 19-year-old joined the Bundesliga side on a season-long loan in September after enduring a frustrating five-month spell at Marseille earlier in the year.

This was supposed to be the loan move to reinvigorate one of England’s best young forwards, at a club well-versed in doing exactly that.

It has been revealed that nwaneri became the fifth Englishman aged 21 or under to sign for Dortmund in the past decade, following in the footsteps of Jadon Sancho, Jude and Jobe Bellingham, and Jamie Gittens. The stars seemed aligned for Nwaneri to shine.

But the opposite has happened. Having impressed and forced a Hoffenheim own goal off the bench on his Dortmund debut, Nwaneri started the team’s next four Bundesliga matches, but was hooked off around the hour mark in each one. The teenager has not made a starting XI since a goalless draw with Union Berlin on October 17.

It is understood Arsenal – who host Dortmund in the Champions League tonight – are closely monitoring the situation around Nwaneri’s lack of minutes, and there is a January recall clause in his contract. The clause was initially inserted as insurance in case an attacking injury crisis arose at Arsenal. Nwaneri's lack of minutes wasn't expected.

Ethan Nwaneri is on loan at Borussia Dortmund from Arsenal but has struggled for minutes – he last started a match on October 17.

The 19-year-old is one of the most talented youngsters to emerge from Arsenal's prolific Hale End academy, but his career is in danger of stalling on loan in Germany.

So why isn’t his move at Dortmund, a club that made their name by developing young players, working out?

Sources indicate that well, Nwaneri's short career so far has been a complicated one, featuring enormous highs and challenging hurdles. To understand his trajectory, you have to look back at his time at Hale End.

Having risen through the academy rapidly upon joining aged eight, Nwaneri burst onto the first-team scene in September 2022 against Brentford, becoming the youngest player to appear in the Premier League, aged 15 years and 181 days.

Mikel Arteta still values the player but hinted on Monday that he needs to produce more than just ‘moments’.

‘You can have patches, but to find that consistency and to play a substantial amount of minutes and have a huge impact in big football clubs like Arsenal or Dortmund, it's extremely difficult,’ he mentioned.

‘That's the reality. You can just shine in moments, but moments are not enough. Now you need to show the consistency. Ethan has the capacity and the mentality to do that, and it takes some time.’.

There's a feeling at Arsenal that Nwaneri has time on his side and shouldn’t be written off. He signed a five-year deal in August 2025 after all, with a plan to fully integrate the attacker into the first-team squad. His brother Emerson, 16, is thriving with the Under 18s.

However, if Nwaneri were to be sold in future, he would, as an academy graduate, generate pure profit on Arsenal's accounts.

‘His time at Borussia has been a disappointment so far because he was brought in to help immediately after Giannis Konstantelias tore his ACL,’ states Sebastian Wessling, who has covered Dortmund for 15 years at the Funke Media Group.

‘They tried to bring Nwaneri in, the summer before. So having tracked and spoken to him previously, they thought he would be ideal for short-term help. But he really hasn’t been that, it’s not worked out well so far.

‘He’s found it difficult to contribute with goals, assists, or just generally in Dortmund’s offensive game.

Industry observers note that ‘What the coach is looking for is a player to make a lot of runs in behind. Whereas Nwaneri looks to drop deep and have time on the ball, which the manager, Niko Kovac, isn’t looking for.’.

'He lacks confidence and I think that shows in his play,' claims Dortmund expert Sebastian Wessling of Nwaneri.

There is still a serious player in Nwaneri, as seen in his two assists for England Under 21s in their 3-2 victory over France last week.

Nwaneri's lack of confidence and progress feel striking. This summer, he joined England's pre-World Cup training camp in Florida, and was an unused substitute in the warm-up match against New Zealand. Nwaneri was alongside Bournemouth's Alex Scott, Fulham's Josh King and Liverpool's Rio Ngumoha – both Scott and Ngumoha have since made their senior England debuts, while King made Thomas Tuchel's squad this month. All three are flourishing as Nwaneri struggles to even feature.

To make matters worse for him, back at Arsenal 16-year-old Max Dowman is competing for a place in the starting XI. Nwaneri may have bundles of talent, but he is yet to fully kick on.

Sources indicate that wessling adds: ‘He lacks confidence and I think that highlights in his play. Niko wants him to be brave on the pitch, but he plays it very safe.

Industry observers note that ‘When he did feature, he often played short passes and didn’t advance Dortmund’s play. He’s not a total disappointment, but he hasn’t really contributed.’.

There is still a serious player in Nwaneri, as seen in his two assists for England Under 21s in their 3-2 victory over France last week. He is eligible to feature at the Emirates tonight, and will be desperate to show Arsenal what they are missing.

In any case, his next two months at Dortmund will reveal plenty about his future. It’s now about consistency – more than mere ‘moments’.

Il Torino con il Napoli fa una partita diversa. La rifà con noi o no? Noi l’abbiamo preparata ma non sappiamo come vengono ad affrontarci ma il dna rimane quello.

Continuare così, essere bravi a perdere meno giocatori possibili.

Doekhi e Leite sono di valore. Sutalo giocava nell’Ajax abituato a un calcio di palleggio. Contro Il Lecce nel primo tempo eravamo lenti non era un problema tecnico.

#153114. Tech Report: Watch out, AlphaFold: Claude and ChatGPT’s newly introduced biology skills wow scientists

Tech Report: Watch out, AlphaFold: Claude and ChatGPT’s newly introduced biology skills wow scientists

📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (961 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nature

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Accurately predicting protein structures has been the preserve of specialist artificial-intelligence tools such as AlphaFold — but now general-purpose models are catching up.
  • According to recent reports, earlier this month, Xinming Tu set out to test what artificial-intelligence models know about proteins.
  • It has been revealed that he left the analysis to run overnight and woke up shocked at the results.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Accurately predicting protein structures has been the preserve of specialist artificial-intelligence tools such as AlphaFold — but now general-purpose models are catching up. Credit: EMBL-EBI (CC0).

According to recent reports, earlier this month, Xinming Tu set out to test what artificial-intelligence models know about proteins. Tu, a researcher at an AI biology manufacturer called Phylo in South San Francisco, California, asked large language models (LLMs) from OpenAI, Anthropic and Google to predict the sequences of obscure bacterial proteins.

It has been revealed that he left the analysis to run overnight and woke up shocked at the results. The latest versions of Anthropic’s Claude models had outperformed other LLMs — including specialized protein-language models, which are trained on vast troves of sequence data and designed for such tasks.

Scientists are using AI to dream up revolutionary upcoming proteins.

Scientists are using AI to dream up revolutionary upcoming proteins.

When Tu and Leo Chen, a computational biologist at Harvard Medical School in Boston, Massachusetts, shared the results in a 16 November blog post, it set off a frenzy among computational biologists to see what other protein biology LLMs such as Claude could do. For instance, Tu, Chen and others have found that the tool could perform a key step in protein-structure prediction.

And on 24 November, OpenAI announced that its latest language models had successfully designed latest proteins, some of which behaved as expected when they were made and tested in the laboratory. The results hint that the latest LLMs might be gaining a sophisticated understanding of protein biology.

Sources indicate that the research has kicked off a debate over the future of biological AI. Some scientists predict that ‘general purpose’ models such as Claude and ChatGPT will eventually outperform specialist tools such as AlphaFold at tasks including protein-structure prediction and design.

“We want to see a world where a scientist can just describe in natural language what they want a ChatGPT model to do, and the model can just be infinitely flexible and design exactly what the person wants,” notes Joy Jiao, who leads life-sciences research at OpenAI in San Francisco, California.

But some researchers question the extent to which LLMs are learning underlying lessons in protein biology. They suggest that some of the models’ abilities could be the result of regurgitating training data.

Sources indicate that the unveiling of AlphaFold2, Google DeepMind’s blockbuster AI tool for protein-structure prediction, in 2020, launched a revolution in biological AI. There is now a vast ecosystem of software — much of it open source — for modelling different properties of proteins, such as how they interact with potential drugs, and for designing latest proteins.

Researchers have begun using LLMs to orchestrate these specialist models, but the LLMs have been used mostly as a time-saving measure, says Martin Pačesa, a structural biologist at the University of Zurich in Switzerland. “In most cases, a specialist will always perform better than a generalist for a given task,” he says.

Five protein-design questions that still challenge AI.

Five protein-design questions that still challenge AI.

Sources indicate that to see if an LLM could stand in for specialist protein-design tools, Jiao and her colleagues asked an OpenAI model called GPT-6.2 to design 3D protein structures capable of binding to five biological targets, including proteins implicated in cancer and immune conditions. After the LLMs generated the designs, the researchers used a specialist AI tool to determine a corresponding genetic sequence. Lab experiments confirmed that around 11% of designs were able to bind to their target.

In other experiments, the OpenAI team showed that its LLMs could design protein sequences, redesign existing antibodies, and do other tasks typically performed by specialist tools. In some cases, the LLM performed as well as some specialist tools, and in others, such as predicting the 3D structure of proteins, it was far off. OpenAI researchers describe the work in a blog post and technical paper.

According to recent reports, jiao emphasizes that the work is a proof of principle, and that specialized AI tools were still needed for key steps. But Masatoshi Uehara, an OpenAI researcher who was part of the effort, thinks that LLMs will only get better at protein biology. “I believe the large language model can technically beat every specialized model in each capability,” he says.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Published: 09:00 EST, 24 November 2026 | Updated: 12:29 EST, 24 November 2026.

They had a World Cup winner in defence, Superman in their squad and a Sex Pistol in charge of recruitment.

There's a clue in the name, but Hollywood United must have been the wildest, most star-studded pub football team of all time.

Ray Winstone, Jason Statham, Mike Myers and Vinnie Jones all turned out for a team that grew out of a gathering of British expats at the Cat & Fiddle pub in the late Eighties.

It being Hollywood, they travelled to matches by private jet and they even took on David Beckham in a charity match.

Now, as the Sex Pistols prepare to embark on a tour marking the 50th anniversary of their debut single, guitarist Steve Jones has revealed how he assembled the extraordinary side on Hollywood's Sunset Boulevard.

Among those who pulled on the shirt were France's World Cup-winning defender Frank Leboeuf, former Scotland captain Richard Gough and Brandon Routh, the American actor who played the superhero in the 2006 film Superman Returns.

Routh was given no special treatment by his team-mates, who would mockingly shout ‘Superman!’ whenever he made a mistake.

Hollywood United is the world's most famous pub team - featuring a littany of high-profile stars.

Created by British expat and Sex Pistols star Steve Jones (right), United have rubbed shoulders with the likes of David Beckham.

Vinnie Jones, meanwhile, had apparently lost none of the competitive instincts that characterised his career in English football.

In 2002, it was reported that he had been sent off just 15 seconds after coming on as a substitute in a Hollywood United friendly.

Anthony LaPaglia, the Australian actor who starred in the hit television series Without a Trace, was their goalkeeper.

There were members of the Sex Pistols, The Cult and Def Leppard, as well as actors such as Ralf Little.

But there were also rather less celebrated footballers.

‘The start of it was with me and Anthony LaPaglia; he was a goalie, and from there it turned into Hollywood United,’ Jones told the Telegraph.

‘We always used to play in a league with a bunch of regular blokes, carpenters and so on, then we got a few more faces who wanted to start kicking about with us like Vinnie Jones.’.

The two Joneses met in a video shop in Los Angeles and the former Wimbledon hardman, who had embarked on a film career with Lock, Stock and Two Smoking Barrels, needed little persuasion to join.

‘He was up for a laugh, and he knows where to put a ball. Most of the team were amateurs, but we were decent and reached a certain level.’.

In November 2007, Hollywood United took on Beckham's LA Galaxy in a charity match.

England manager Steve McClaren had flown to California to assess Beckham's fitness ahead of a European Championship qualifier against Croatia. It's not clear whether he attended the match, which Hollywood United lost 12-4. Beckham scored twice, as did Leboeuf and over 5,000 spectators raised more than $100,000 for victims of the California wildfires.

Steve Jones, now 71, had himself broken one of football's golden rules by changing his allegiance.

Vinnie Jones (left) and Ray Winstone (right) have turned out for the amateur football team.

Actor Anthony LaPaglia lets the team travel on his private jet to matches across America.

Having followed QPR as a schoolboy in west London and also been associated with Fulham, he became a Chelsea supporter after moving to California and getting sober.

Chelsea's games were available on American television and his lifelong friend and fellow Sex Pistol Paul Cook was already a diehard Blues fan.

Hollywood United played at Griffith Park, beneath the famous Hollywood sign, but their adventures would take them considerably further afield.

LaPaglia would arrange private jets to transport the players to matches.

Gough recalls one trip when the team flew to Vancouver for a charity match before heading straight to the Mexican resort of Puerto Vallarta to play a side of former Mexico internationals.

Vinnie Jones also told the Guardian in 2007 that Hollywood United had fielded nine former international footballers in a single match.

The club's ranks included former Liverpool and Newcastle defender Barry Venison and United States internationals Alexi Lalas and Eric Wynalda.

Winstone, a lifelong West Ham fan, found playing in the Californian heat rather more demanding than he had anticipated.

He later recalled being so exhausted by the time the ball reached him that he was barely able to kick it. And he wasn't particularly impressed by the willingness of former Chelsea defender Leboeuf to pass the ball, describing the Frenchman as a greedy player.

Among those watching from the touchline was the actor John Hurt, who was in town filming Indiana Jones and the Kingdom of the Crystal Skull with Winstone.

Some of the rock stars had impressive footballing pedigrees.

Ian Astbury, the lead singer of The Cult, had played boys' club football in Glasgow alongside future Everton and Scotland striker Graeme Sharp.

Gough, meanwhile, struck up a conversation with a team-mate from Northern Ireland without having the slightest idea he was Vivian Campbell, the guitarist of Def Leppard.

Sex Pistol Jones, who has lived in Los Angeles for more than 40 years, is returning to Britain next month for a tour marking the 50th anniversary of the release of Anarchy in the UK.

He still regularly attends football matches whenever he is back in England, although he has little time for the corporate hospitality enjoyed by many of his celebrity contemporaries.

‘I don't care where I sit, but I'm not interested in sitting in some box with a bunch of t***ers.’.
