Spitting row mars feisty Millwall-West Ham clash

📅 19 Sep 2026 | ⏱️ 27 min read (5417 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~27 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • A spitting row marred the 100th Millwall-West Ham United derby and first for 14 years.
  • Taty Castellanos was facing trial by video after being accused of spitting on Filip Marschall during Saturday’s febrile 2-2 draw at the Den.
  • Millwall goalkeeper Marschall made the allegation to referee Paul Tierney, who was expected to include it in an official report that would then be assessed by the Football Association.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A spitting row marred the 100th Millwall-West Ham United derby and first for 14 years.

Taty Castellanos was facing trial by video after being accused of spitting on Filip Marschall during Saturday’s febrile 2-2 draw at the Den.

Millwall goalkeeper Marschall made the allegation to referee Paul Tierney, who was expected to include it in an official report that would then be assessed by the Football Association.

Spitting on an opponent is punishable with a six-match ban.

Telegraph Sport has been told West Ham striker Castellanos denies he spat on Marschall and believes he will be vindicated by video footage of the incident.

Lying little prick. Taty didn't spit ❌ pic.twitter.com/5vYxOtKqof.

Millwall manager Alex Neil stated after the game that fourth official Lewis Smith had confirmed a spitting accusation had been made.

Asked if he had spoken to Marschall about the claim, Neil replied: “I haven’t asked him about it. But it’s like anything else; I’m sure there’ll be footage of it, or not of it, if it didn’t happen.

“I’d be extremely surprised if Fil’s made an accusation and nothing’s happened. But that’s not really for me to deal with; I’m sure the authorities will deal with that.”.

West Ham manager Nuno Espírito Santo mentioned: “I’m aware of the allegation. I didn’t see the image; I didn’t speak with Taty. I cannot go much further on that.”.

He added: “I’m going to try to look at the images.”.

There were also ugly scenes at full time when players had to be separated at the end of a derby that had been at the centre of an unprecedented police operation.

There were six arrests as of 4pm on Saturday for offences including tailgating, assault on a police officer and entering or attempting to enter a stadium while intoxicated.

Eleven men were also arrested at around 7.15pm on Friday on suspicion of conspiracy to commit criminal damage.

The group, believed to be Millwall fans, were detained in the vicinity of a known West Ham supporters’ pub in Stratford.

Saturday’s fixture was subject to a five-mile dispersal zone, the largest ever for a football match in London, with officers granted special powers to stop and search people and vehicles without reasonable suspicion and to remove anyone causing disorder.

Riot police were out in force outside the ground, with dog units and mounted officers among 400 personnel deployed – roughly quadruple the usual number for a game there.

Those and other measures – including the use of live facial recognition, a strict segregation policy and a 12.30pm kick-off to minimise supporters’ pre-match drinking time – prevented a repeat of the kind of violence which has marred this fixture down the years.

West Ham fans also received a police escort to a game that saw both sets of supporters hurl foul-mouthed insults at each other throughout.

Plans to keep rival spectators apart after the match were reportedly tested by scuffles that broke out as people left the ground.

This rivalry was forged in different circumstances from most derby confrontations. There is none of the religious divide of Celtic and Rangers, or the politics of Barcelona against Real Madrid, or the spat over title-winning superiority of Manchester United and Liverpool. This is a tale of proximity, an internecine feud.

According to recent reports, “There’s no politics, no nationality, nothing like that,” claims Nick Hart, who hosts the weekly podcast Achtung! Millwall. “We’re very similar people, from the same backgrounds, same communities. But it’s in the Millwall supporter’s DNA for West Ham to be the ultimate rivals. Nobody else comes into the equation. You’re brought up on this stuff. It’s your history.”.

It has been revealed that though possibly more recent history than might be suggested by the two clubs’ early foundations. The hostility that West Ham will face at the Den is no more about dockland rivalry, north-south London disputes or strike-breaking than the animosity when Manchester United visit Anfield is caused by the building of the Manchester Ship Canal.

In a recent development, “It really is about the hooligan era,” indicates a podcaster who uses the pseudonym Former West Ham Employee on the West Ham Way podcast. “The two clubs had notorious fanbases. And they grated. It came about through vying to be the No 1, battling to see who had the hardest mob. Whenever we’ve played – or even been in close proximity – things have happened.”.

Jake Cooper on making the 500th appearance of his career against West Ham today! 👏Watch all the action with NOW! https://t.co/56JOZ0NPsr pic.twitter.com/lTzXOwXhxd.

Industry observers note that there have only been 18 meetings between these fierce rivals since the Second World War, but absence has certainly not made the heart grow fonder. Here are some of the feud’s most notable flashpoints.

Industry observers note that at the 1972 testimonial in honour of Harry Cripps – the renowned Millwall hard man – police horses were sent on to the pitch after West Ham supporters entered the home section at The Den. Fighting spilt over into the streets surrounding the ground.

An even bleaker turn came in 1976, when Millwall fan Ian Pratt died in a skirmish with West Ham fans at Upcoming Cross station that led to his fall under a train.

Leaflets were later handed out in the Den’s Cold Blow Lane end with a grainy picture of Pratt and a declaration in capital letters: “A West Ham fan must die next week to avenge him.”.

Millwall plundered four goals on Mothering Sunday in 2004 as Tim Cahill’s double helped them to a 4-1 victory over West Ham at the Den in an incident-filled derby.

According to recent reports, the hosts missed a penalty and had another saved by Stephen Bywater, who was later sent off. Violence followed in the stands and the match was named “The Mothers’ Day Massacre”.

Mother's Day Massacre ⏮️A 4-1 victory over The Hammers back in 2004. pic.twitter.com/TLi7xkcVJG.

A hundred West Ham and Millwall supporters clashed during a screening of England’s 2006 World Cup match against Paraguay in Canada Square, which led to 16 injuries and one hospitalisation.

The clubs’ League Cup meeting in 2009 at Upton Park was listed as Category Five by police, the most serious risk of violence, and resulted in a Millwall supporter being stabbed in Priory Road, near the ground.

The Metropolitan Police stated that “planned” scuffles, which involved more than 100 fans, appeared to have been caused by fans without tickets to the game.

Industry observers note that just spotted one Millwall fan outside the ground in blue boxing gloves. He is also wearing what appear to be slippers, so not sure what that means….

Nuno Espirito Santo has only been through the door at West Ham for a matter of months, but he insisted he is fully aware of the significance of today’s fixture.

According to recent reports, when asked about his perception of the rivalry, Nuno said: “Since the fixture list came out, this date has been [key], for both of the clubs. It’s special, special game. We look forward to go and compete against a good team.

“It’s a different game from all of the other games, it’s a special game, the atmosphere will be different… Steve [Potts, first-team coach and former West Ham player] has been involved in many of these games, he’s constantly speaking about how special it is for West Ham fans, so we have a lot of information and we are fully aware of the importance of the game.

According to recent reports, on potential unrest between fans and the significant police presence, Nuno added: “What we want most is that everything goes well, both fans supporting their teams and no conflict. We have people inside the club who are taking care of that. We have to focus on our tasks.”.

The gaffer on tomorrow's fixture ⬇️ pic.twitter.com/6NG6t4t4Fn.

Sources indicate that riot police are very much out in force outside The Den today for the 100th competitive derby between Millwall and West Ham United and first for 14 years. Dog units and mounted officers can been seen patrolling the perimeter of the ground, with 400 personnel deployed to stop violence erupting between rival fans – roughly quadruple the usual number for a fixture here. There has been no sign of any trouble with less than an hour to go before kick-off.

The game has been scheduled for 12.30pm to minimise supporters’ pre-match drinking time, although plenty of fans have been nursing pints before entering the ground. Other measures in place include the use of live facial recognition cameras, while a dispersal order has been imposed covering a large area around the stadium. Police were also planning to escort West Ham fans from South Bermondsey station, which will also be closed to home supporters for up to an hour after full-time. The latter measure has been deemed safer than holding the 1,800 away fans back following the game.

In a recent development, the Millwall-West Ham derby is one of the most notorious in English football and was most recently marred by serious violence when the sides met at Upton Park for a League Cup tie back in 2009. One man was stabbed and the match itself was interrupted on three occasions by fans invading the pitch.

The Metropolitan Police will have 400 officers on the streets of east London for this match – about four times the norm for a Championship fixture – and it has enforced a Section 35 dispersal order in the area highlighted on the map below.

A Section 35 order authorises a Police Constable and a Police Community Support Officer in uniform to “exclude a person from an area for a period of up to 48 hours with an Inspector’s authority”.

Good morning and welcome to our live coverage of the highly anticipated Championship match between Millwall and West Ham United as the two clubs meet officially for the 100th time. This fixture has not been staged since 2012, and the intervening 14 years have done little to temper the ill-feeling between their passionate supporters, who will be anxious to claim bragging rights over their Dockers Derby rivals. The Metropolitan Police have placed a Section 35 dispersal order in the area surrounding The Den and will deploy 400 officers on the streets of east London.

Acrimony between the two clubs has existed since the late 19th century when Millwall Athletic, originally Rovers, battled it out against Thames Ironworks, later renamed West Ham at the Athletic and Memorial Grounds. Sixty of the two clubs’ 99 meetings came between 1899 and 1915, and while they played just seven times between 1946 and 1987, the irregularity of the game only added to its mystique, which has often spilt over into the ugly.

Both head coaches spoke at length about the significance of today’s match, with Alex Neil, in the Millwall dugout, describing it as an encounter that means “absolutely everything” but imploring his players to keep “cool heads”. His counterpart Nuno Espírito Santo revealed that he had been well advised about the game’s importance by Steve Potts, his first-team coach and former West Ham player.

According to recent reports, since the club’s last meeting in 2012, West Ham have ascended into the Premier League, moved into the London Stadium and won the Uefa Conference League, only falling back into England’s second tier last summer where Millwall have remained for all but two seasons. The Lions brushed maddeningly close to promotion in their last campaign as they pushed for an automatic spot until the very last weekend of the regular season before falling to Hull City in the play-off semi-finals.

It has been revealed that much of the pre-match talk will centre on the clubs’ long-standing rivalry, but beneath the bile and belligerence is an intriguing football match between two sides. Millwall are missing 11 first-team players and face the daunting task of stopping a West Ham side who have found their feet in the Championship, scoring 16 goals in their last four league matches.

Sources indicate that A Radio Napoli Centrale, nel corso di Sempre Con Te è intervenuto Enzo Bucchioni: “Un voto alto per il Napoli, la miglior partita stagionale. Lo aspettavamo così dall’inizio. Una prestazione inattesa, finalmente però si è ritrovato l’orgoglio di una grande squadra. Si era visto in stagione qualche sprazzo di Napoli convincente. Il pareggio con il City ha un sapore differente. Non era atteso, può essere questa la ripartenza vera? C’è da augurarsi di sì. Le prossime sono alla portata. Il Napoli deve segnare di più e subire di meno? Secondo me subire di meno. È mancato il sacrificio degli attaccanti. Se non danno una mano per primi, qualsiasi fase difensiva va in difficoltà. È uscito Lang, la fase difensiva non la faceva, era pigro. Quando perdi palla devi andare con determinazione sul pallone ed è successo. La fase difensiva non funzionava per questo. Le squadre di Allegri hanno sempre avuto queste caratteristiche, ma non riusciva a farsi capire. Come vedo le parole di Allegri su De Bruyne? La posizione di De Bruyne la sappiamo, gli piace un altro calcio. Spero che contro il City si sia divertito, penso che ci sia stato anche un confronto. Un allenatore che si sbilancia lo vedo come segnale importante. Allegri ha ripreso la barca, quel tipo di calcio con il baricentro basso e rincorse all’indietro non faccia parte del bagaglio di molti giocatori. Anche Allegri ha provato a fare altre cose, ma non gli erano riuscite. Ieri abbiamo visto Allegri con la faccia giusta”.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Mikel Arteta remarked David Raya’s shoulder injury isn’t ‘too serious’, sparking hope that the goalkeeper could return within weeks.
  • Sources indicate that raya was forced off in the 70th minute of Arsenal’s 2-2 draw against Newcastle on Saturday at St James’ Park, hurting his left shoulder in a collision with William Osula.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By ISAAN KHAN, REPORTER and WILL GRIFFEE.

Published: 09:10 EST, 23 November 2026 | Updated: 12:39 EST, 24 November 2026.

Mikel Arteta remarked David Raya’s shoulder injury isn’t ‘too serious’, sparking hope that the goalkeeper could return within weeks.

Sources indicate that raya was forced off in the 70th minute of Arsenal’s 2-2 draw against Newcastle on Saturday at St James’ Park, hurting his left shoulder in a collision with William Osula. He looked in agony as he left the pitch.

His No 2 Kepa Arrizabalaga is instead expected to play for the north London club in their Champions League match against Borussia Dortmund on Tuesday.

Though Arteta confirmed Raya doesn’t require surgery and didn’t yet rule him out for Sunday’s Premier League clash against Manchester City.

‘He’s (Raya) not fit for tomorrow, but it doesn’t look too serious,’ remarked Arteta. ‘We need some more tests tomorrow, but it’s quite encouraging. It seems to be better than expected.

It has been revealed that ‘We expected something much worse because he could almost not handle the amount of pain he had. The first test shows something much more encouraging.

Arsenal's No 1 David Raya underwent an MRI scan the day after going off against Newcastle.

‘There is no need for surgery, which was the main fear because that would have ruled him out for months.’.

In a recent development, asked whether Raya could play at home to Man City, he added: ‘Tomorrow we’ll have more tests and we will know. I think we’ve seen what David brings to the team as well.

It has been revealed that ‘That’s why we are very protective with Kepa and (third-choice) Illan (Meslier). Everybody needs to be ready because these things unfortunately happen.’.

Raya has been sensational for the Premier League champions and his absence is likely to hurt the best defensive unit.

It has been revealed that 'That's a massive worry,' Ian Wright noted on Sky Sports when the stopper went down. 'I don't want to say I'm petrified simply because Kepa is in goal, he's the guy who has got to try and keep the goals out for us now.

'But yeah, that is a massive blow. Someone like him, Declan Rice, Gabriel, it is very tough to replace those guys.'.

Meanwhile, Bruno Guimaraes said Arteta is ‘crazy’ about the small details that will take him to ‘another level’.

Since his summer move from Newcastle, the 29-year-old has scored vital goals against Sunderland and Leeds - but is yet to complete a full 90 minutes in the Premier League.

Raya hit the turf in pain and went off the pitch clutching his arm to indicate that something serious had happened.

‘I now definitely understand my role in the team and the way Mikel wants me to play but I can still play much better,’ said the Brazilian.

‘I think Mikel (Arteta) is unbelievable. He as a manager is so focused on small details, the way you control the ball, the way that you cannot be aligned with your opposite side.

‘Some details I have never heard before, I just found out with him here. He is crazy a little bit about these small details and I try and take (in) as much as I can because he is so passionate about them.

‘He showed me some clips (from when I was) in Newcastle and some clips here, where he thinks I can do things differently. He's trying to take me to another level.’.

According to recent reports, arsenal's clash with Borussia Dortmund on Tuesday night will feature a fresh innovation for its TV audience watching on Prime Video. Called 'Progressive Actions' it highlights the passes and ball carries that drive a team up the pitch, and the often-unsung players behind them. Developed by Prime Video's team of producers, engineers, AI experts, and on-air analysts, Progressive Actions is the first Prime Insight built specifically for the UEFA Champions League. It joins the growing suite of features on Prime Vision, the alternate feed which serves as a laboratory and incubator for new features that often advance to the main broadcast.

Progressive Actions is built on proprietary AI-powered models that identify a Progressive Action based on how far the ball travels in each phase of the pitch, with the threshold becoming shorter closer to the opposition goal where defences are more compact and space is harder to find. The metric mirrors the data used behind the scenes at Europe's elite clubs, yet has historically been difficult to show during a live broadcast. As a player makes a Progressive Action, an on-pitch graphic will show where the action started and ended, the player involved, and the distance the ball advanced, allowing fans to see the game as a coaching team would, in real time.

'Prime Vision is where we develop latest features that shine a spotlight on the metrics, actions and players that impact a game most, yet aren't always captured by traditional statistics or broadcast techniques,' noted Andrew Hornett, Director of Live Sports Production for Europe at Prime Video.

'Every team has players whose influence goes far beyond the scoresheet, the ones doing the crucial work in the build-up, moving the ball forward two or three passes before an assist. Progressive Actions is designed to capture that impact, measuring and visualising these actions during a live broadcast. Fans will see them in real time as they happen, but we'll also aggregate the data across the game, so you can see which players have had the biggest impact on the match.'.

Industry observers note that the feature will debut in the UK and Ireland on Tuesday and will also be available for fans in Germany and Italy. Fans can access Prime Vision, with features including Progressive Actions, via their remote from the match detail page or the in-game menu during any live UCL fixture on Prime Video.

Progressive Actions is the first Prime Insight built from the ground up specifically for Prime Video's UEFA Champions League coverage, and sits alongside Tactical Map, Momentum, Physical Insights, Advanced Analytics, Passing Options, and Player ID in Prime Vision's growing suite of features designed to take football fans closer to the game, all available on the alternate feed during every UEFA Champions League match live on Prime Video. Prime Insights were first developed for Prime Video's coverage of Thursday Night Football, its exclusive weekly NFL package in the US, where AI-powered features including the award-winning Defensive Alerts have become a staple of the coverage, advancing from the alternate feed to the main broadcast each week.

Industry News: All that money spent and Spurs do not have a proper striker or goalkeeper

📅 20 Sep 2026 | ⏱️ 29 min read (5884 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~29 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that for all the money spent, Tottenham Hotspur have started this season without a reliable out-and-out striker and short of a top goalkeeper.
  • Industry observers note that we keep hearing that Dominic Solanke will be the man to give Spurs a goalscoring threat, but how long has it been since we have seen him fully fit and firing?
  • Antonin Kinsky may have finished last season well, but there was further evidence in this defeat that he is well short of the best goalkeepers in the division.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that for all the money spent, Tottenham Hotspur have started this season without a reliable out-and-out striker and short of a top goalkeeper. And it is already costing them dear.

Industry observers note that we keep hearing that Dominic Solanke will be the man to give Spurs a goalscoring threat, but how long has it been since we have seen him fully fit and firing? Maybe not since his Bournemouth days.

Antonin Kinsky may have finished last season well, but there was further evidence in this defeat that he is well short of the best goalkeepers in the division.

It is a puzzle how Tottenham signed 10 fresh players, but did not upgrade two of the most vital positions on the pitch.

In a recent development, only when Aston Villa were out of sight and the game was effectively over did Spurs break their Premier League goal drought. And even then it was a midfielder, Conor Gallagher, and a defender, Jan Paul van Hecke, who were on target.

Solanke had gone off just before Villa scored their second goal, which highlighted the significant difference between the two sides on Saturday and where Spurs are badly lacking.

Zion Suzuki, the Villa goalkeeper, rolled out a long ball upfield, Nicolas Jackson managed to lay it off for Johan Mazambi, who returned the favour. Jackson touched the ball past Micky van de Ven’s challenge before beating Kinsky with a well-struck shot.

Spurs are stunned as Nicolas Jackson doubles Aston Villa's lead 😳📺 Stream now on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/il7NKbgFCQ.

Sources indicate that it was an excellent goal, but Kinsky got a good hand to it and a top goalkeeper would have pushed it around the post. On the evidence of the first half, when he made four saves, Suzuki would have also stopped the ball creeping into the net.

Sources indicate that suzuki cost Villa in the region of £30m and he looks a more than able replacement for Emiliano Martínez. Spurs, on the other hand, have not had a top-class goalkeeper since Hugo Lloris and it is a puzzle that so much faith has been placed in Kinsky.

Spurs spent most of the summer firmly denying any links to Jackson before Villa signed him from Chelsea for an initial £47.5m that could rise to £65m. Given the London club paid an initial £75m for Sávio and committed to a £60m obligation to make Omar Marmoush’s season-long loan permanent, Jackson might have been a relative bargain for them.

According to recent reports, asked if Tottenham had made a massive mistake by failing to sign a proper number nine, head coach Robert De Zerbi mentioned: “The transfer market was long. The situation changed many times. There was also the financial rules, at the end of the transfer market. And we had to respect the rules.

Recent findings suggest that “We didn’t sell the players who we thought, in the beginning, there was the possibility, the chance to sell. There are a lot of reasons. I think the club and the coach, we are not sleeping, we know the characteristics of the players, we know everything. And if we didn’t make any different decisions, it was because we couldn’t.”.

That sounded a bit like excuses, but De Zerbi did not put up much of a defence for Solanke as he mentioned: “We need more from him, for sure, but he’s one of my players. I like Dom as a player and I stay with him until the end. He needs to stay better, to feel better. The physical condition is not good enough, but it’s normal for him. Maybe he is not confident enough in himself at this moment, because he’s much better than this. I think we can’t say everything is bad, but it’s not enough.”.

Sources indicate that it was Sávio who forced Suzuki into making a brilliant double save from him in the first half, when Tottenham were well on top. The Japan international also stopped an Archie Gray shot from squirming through his legs and into the net, and dived to turn another Sávio effort around his right-hand post.

It has been revealed that good afternoon and welcome to our coverage of today’s bottom-of-the-table epic: Tottenham Hotspur vs Aston Villa. This tie is incidentally the match-up between the last two winners of the Europa League, though so far neither of them have looked like European champions.

It is definitely fair to say that this season has not started the way either of these teams would have wanted, as the host side currently sit in what is apparently their favourite position – 17th – and the visitors are all the way in 19th, only above Coventry.

Despite getting off to a fairly convincing start in the Champions League with a 3-2 win over Club Brugge, Villa only scored their first league goal last week in their match against Nottingham Forest, though it was a futile one as they still lost 2-1 at Villa Park.

Sources indicate that tottenham meanwhile are still waiting for their first league goal, despite putting one past Liverpool in their 3-1 defeat in the Carabao Cup third round. With no European football and already out of one cup competition, Roberto De Zerbi has only the FA Cup in January and the rest of the league season to drag Spurs out of the perpetual rut they appear to find themselves in. They sit only one point above Villa as they have been able to see out two 0-0 draws – against Everton and Nottingham Forest – instead of one.

There has been plenty of talk about the money spent by both teams, without the results yet to show for it. The total sits around half a billion between them, adding to the mounting pressure on both De Zerbi and Unai Emery. Summer signings for both teams have struggled to land, something which will not be helped by the upcoming international break.

But before then, the teams have 90 minutes to try and get their seasons up and running, and we will be bringing you the team news, lineups and all the action from the match! Stay tuned!

Fabio Cannavaro, capitano dell'Italia campione del mondo nel 2006 e vincitore del Pallone d'Oro, intervistato da La Gazzetta dello Sport ha analizzato la corsa scudetto, soffermandosi anche sulla situazione della Lazio e sul mercato di gennaio.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM.

Recent findings suggest that L'Inter è fuori concorso per il livello della rosa, ma aspettiamo. La Roma ha fame, un sistema di gioco definito e un attaccante che fa gol. Il Como non è più una sorpresa e sono contento per Gattuso: tutti pensavano che la sua esperienza all'estero fosse un tragico errore, invece è migliorato come allenatore e persona. Spero regga fino a gennaio, poi vediamo se il club gli comprerà qualcuno.

Palma? Ha grande potenziale, ma deve migliorare le letture e l'uno contro uno in area. Vediamo, di sicuro sa giocare a calcio. L'Italia prende tanti gol, davvero tanti, ma non è questione di coppia: bisogna ragionare di squadra. Devi far capire ai giocatori che non sono cavalli e che il pressing deve essere orientato. Spalletti diceva: 'Se perdi tempo tra il pensare di pressare e l'andare a pressare, sei già in ritardo'. L'Italia è così.

Pakistani astronaut to become first foreign visitor to China’s space station

📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (729 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nature

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Three astronauts will launch aboard China’s Shenzhou-24 spacecraft.Credit: Xinhua/Shutterstock.
  • For the first time, China will send a foreign astronaut to its Tiangong space station.
  • Muhammad Zeeshan Ali, a Pakistani military pilot, is expected to travel to Tiangong on 25 November aboard China’s Shenzhou-24 spacecraft, alongside two Chinese astronauts, known as ‘taikonauts’.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Three astronauts will launch aboard China’s Shenzhou-24 spacecraft.Credit: Xinhua/Shutterstock.

For the first time, China will send a foreign astronaut to its Tiangong space station.

Muhammad Zeeshan Ali, a Pakistani military pilot, is expected to travel to Tiangong on 25 November aboard China’s Shenzhou-24 spacecraft, alongside two Chinese astronauts, known as ‘taikonauts’.

Recent findings suggest that “My first [flight] not only represents myself, but also my country,” Ali told reporters in Mandarin on 24 November at the Jiuquan Satellite Launch Centre in northwest China. Ali has been training intensively in Beijing for the past seven months, including learning Mandarin. He mentioned that he carried “the dream of 250 million Pakistani people” when he entered the training centre.

In a recent development, sending an astronaut to space is “a huge step” for Pakistan’s space aspirations, says Wajiha Iqbal, a lunar scientist at the University of Münster in Germany. The partnership enables Pakistan to “do great science in space”, she adds.

Industry observers note that the mission is also a milestone for China’s space programme. The country’s expanding capabilities now allow it to offer international partners opportunities that few countries can provide on their own, states Yuxuan Jia, who researches China’s foreign policy at the Center for China and Globalization, a think tank in Beijing. The launch signals China’s “aspirations to become a top space power”, Jia says.

Recent findings suggest that shenzhou-24 is expected to be carried into a low-Earth orbit by China’s Long March-2F rocket, which is scheduled to launch from the Jiuquan Satellite Launch Centre at 08:18am local time on 25 November, remarked Zhang Jingbo, a spokesperson of the China Manned Space Programme, at a press conference on 24 November. Shenzhou-24 is expected to automatically dock with Tiangong (which translates as ‘heavenly palace’) around 3.5 hours after reaching orbit.

Ali will stay on Tiangong for about a week before returning to Earth with two of the three taikonauts presently on the station.

China’s successful launch of Mars mission seals global era in deep-space exploration.

China’s successful launch of Mars mission seals global era in deep-space exploration.

Ali will board Shenzhou-24 as a payload specialist responsible mainly for scientific experiments rather than operating the spacecraft. The mission aims to host four biotechnology experiments developed by universities in Pakistan, Amer Gilani, an official at Pakistan’s space agency told newswire Reuters in September. Details about the research have not yet been made public.

According to Zhang, one goal of this mission is to establish a study of how the human body adapts to space flight. Zhu Yangzhu, an astronaut who entered Tiangong in May, will remain aboard the space station for another six months to allow for this experiment to take place, Zhang stated.

Astronauts Muhammad Zeeshan Ali, Wu Yi and Tang Hongbo will travel to China's space station the Tiangong.Credit: CCTV+/VCG via Getty.

  • La vendita sarà preceduta da una promozione riservata agli abbonati Full a 24 gare della stagione 2025/26.
  • In a recent development, la vendita dei biglietti per la partita contro il Milan si articola in tre fasi.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

SSC Napoli comunica che a partire dalle ore 12:00 di venerdì 27 novembre 2026 saranno in vendita i biglietti per Napoli vs Milan , partita di Serie A che si disputerà domenica 13 dicembre alle ore 20:45 allo Stadio Diego Armando Maradona.

La vendita sarà preceduta da una promozione riservata agli abbonati Full a 24 gare della stagione 2025/26.

In a recent development, la vendita dei biglietti per la partita contro il Milan si articola in tre fasi. La prima fase (Fase 1) di vendita sarà riservata ai possessori di Fidelity Card “Fan Stadium Card”. La seconda fase di vendita (Fase 2) sarà riservata ai possessori della Membership Premium SSC Napoli , per la quale il Club riserverà una specifica quota di biglietti. Infine, la terza fase di vendita (Fase 3) sarà libera.

Sources indicate that ricordiamo che la Fidelity Card può essere sviluppata direttamente online al prezzo di 20€ ed è valevole per tre anni. Clicca qui per maggiori informazioni.

Tutti coloro che hanno acquistato una Membership Premium SSCN entro il 31 maggio 2026 avranno la possibilità di mantenere il proprio status e beneficiare dei relativi vantaggi.

Per i nati dopo il 13 dicembre 2012 è prevista, in tutti i settori e in tutte e tre le fasi di vendita, la tariffa combinata Ridotto Under 14 indicata in tabella.

VENDITA PER TIFOSI CON DISABILITÀ PER NAPOLI VS MILAN.

I posti riservati ai tifosi con disabilità saranno prenotabili (fino ad esaurimento dei posti disponibili) a partire dalle ore 16:00 di venerdì 4 dicembre 2026, previa registrazione attraverso la procedura presente al seguente link: https://sscnapoli.it/regolamento-accesso-tifosi-con-disabilita/.

VENDITA PER LE FAMIGLIE (TRIBUNA FAMILY) PER NAPOLI VS MILAN.

I posti riservati alle famiglie (Tribuna Family) saranno acquistabili (fino ad esaurimento dei posti disponibili) a partire dalle ore 16:00 di venerdì 4 dicembre 2026, online e presso i punti vendita abilitati ( clicca qui per consultare l’elenco) e previa esibizione della documentazione indicata al seguente link https://sscnapoli.it/tribuna-family/ . L’inizio della vendita della Tribuna Family è previsto nella Fase 3, pertanto non sarà necessario essere titolari di Fidelity Card.

Questi i prezzi della Tribuna Family:.

La tariffa Under 12 è riservata ai nati dopo il 13 dicembre 2014.

PROMOZIONE ABBONATI COMPLETA 2025/26 (24 GARE).

Dalle ore 12:00 di venerdì 27 novembre 2026 e fino alle ore 23:59 di domenica 29 novembre 2026, gli abbonati Full a 24 gare della stagione 2025/26 potranno utilizzare il numero della Fidelity Card sulla quale è caricato il proprio abbonamento come codice di sblocco per acquistare un biglietto in via prioritaria, alla tariffa Fidelity, in qualsiasi posto e settore disponibile, a favore di un’altra persona in possesso di Carta Fedeltà. Il titolo di ingresso sarà caricato, in modalità digitale, sulla Fidelity Card del destinatario.

FASE 1 – PREVENDITA FIDELITY SSC NAPOLI – TESSERA FAN STADIUM.

It has been revealed that dalle ore 10:00 di lunedì 30 novembre 2026 e fino alle ore 23:59 di giovedì 3 dicembre 2026 (ovvero, in ogni caso, fino ad esaurimento posti), i possessori di Fidelity Card “SSC Napoli Fan Stadium Card” potranno acquistare fino ad un massimo di 4 biglietti in prevendita, ad un prezzo ridotto rispetto a quello applicato durante la Fase 3 (Vendita Libera). I biglietti acquistati nel corso della Fase 1 dovranno necessariamente essere destinati ai tifosi fidelizzati, sulle cui Fidelity Card saranno caricati i biglietti in formato digitale.

FASE 2 – ISCRIZIONE PREMIUM SSC NAPOLI.

Dalle ore 10:00 di venerdì 4 dicembre 2026 e fino alle ore 15:00 di venerdì 4 dicembre (ovvero, in ogni caso, fino ad esaurimento dei posti disponibili), i possessori di una Membership Premium SSC Napoli avranno la possibilità di acquistare 1 biglietto in via prioritaria e ad un prezzo ridotto rispetto a quello applicato durante la Fase 3 (Vendita Libera), nei limiti dei posti messi a tal fine a disposizione dal club. Potranno accedere alla fase di precedenza per l’acquisto di un biglietto tutti i Membri che hanno sottoscritto la Membership Premium entro e non oltre le ore 23:59 di domenica 31 maggio 2026 . I Membri dovranno utilizzare il numero della propria membership, disponibile nella sezione “Il mio Profilo” all’interno dell’area riservata, per poter accedere alla fase di vendita dedicata. Nel corso della fase 2, il biglietto potrà essere acquistato dal Socio online e potrà essere caricato in formato digitale sulla Fidelity Card “Fan Stadium Card”, qualora l’acquirente ne fosse in possesso, oppure sul portafoglio del proprio smartphone utilizzando la modalità di acquisto Passbook.

In caso di disponibilità residua di biglietti al termine della Fase 2 e salve diverse prescrizioni da parte delle competenti autorità, la fase di vendita libera avrà inizio alle ore 16:00 di venerdì 4 dicembre 2026 e terminerà ad esaurimento posti (ovvero, in ogni caso, al fischio di inizio della Partita). Ogni tifoso potrà acquistare fino ad un massimo di 4 biglietti, con caricamento sulla Fidelity Card o utilizzando la modalità di acquisto Passbook che prevede il caricamento del titolo sul wallet del proprio smartphone. Allo stesso tempo il biglietto potrà essere caricato sulla Fidelity Card oppure emesso in formato cartaceo se l’acquisto avverrà presso uno dei punti vendita abilitati. Fare clic qui per consultare l’elenco.

Per maggiori informazioni sulla modalità Passbook consultare questo link (si apre in una nuova scheda).

In attesa delle decisioni delle Autorità Competenti, la vendita è vietata ai residenti nella regione Lombardia, ad eccezione dei possessori di Fidelity Card SSC Napoli emessa entro il 1° settembre 2026.

I biglietti potranno essere acquistati:.

FASE 1 (Fidelity Card “Fan Stadium Card”).

Il titolo di ingresso sarà caricato, in modalità digitale, sulla Fidelity Card (Fan Stadium Card);.

FASE 2 (Abbonamento Premium SSC Napoli).

Il titolo di ingresso potrà essere caricato, in modalità digitale, sulla Fidelity Card (Fan Stadium Card) qualora disponibile, oppure in modalità Passbook, che prevede il caricamento del titolo sul proprio wallet (non è necessario essere titolari di Fidelity Card).

Il titolo di ingresso potrà essere caricato, in modalità digitale, sulla Fidelity Card (Fan Stadium Card) qualora disponibile, oppure in modalità Passbook, che prevede il caricamento del titolo sul proprio wallet (non è necessario essere titolari di Fidelity Card).

Industry observers note that il link per l’acquisto online dei titoli d’ingresso è disponibile qui. (si apre in una nuova scheda).

FASE 1 (Fidelity Card “Fan Stadium Card”).

Il titolo di ingresso sarà caricato, in modalità digitale, sulla Fidelity Card (Fan Stadium Card).

FASE 2 (Abbonamento Premium SSC Napoli).

Non è possibile usufruire della modalità di acquisto presso i punti vendita.

Il biglietto potrà essere caricato sulla Fidelity Card oppure emesso in formato cartaceo – stampa termica (non è necessario essere titolari di Fidelity Card).

L’elenco dei punti vendita è disponibile qui.

In nessun caso sarà consentito il cambio utilizzatore per i biglietti acquistati.

Si raccomanda di non acquistare i tagliandi in circuiti o canali web diversi da quelli ufficiali e indicati in questo comunicato. La SSC Napoli non risponde di eventuali frodi subite a seguito di acquisti effettuati al di fuori dei canali autorizzati. Inoltre, ogni abuso e/o utilizzo fraudolento dei biglietti sarà punito ai termini di legge.

In attesa delle decisioni delle Autorità Competenti, la vendita dei biglietti potrebbe essere soggetta a limitazioni territoriali.

ACCREDITI PER TESSERATI CONI – FIGC – AIA PER NAPOLI VS MILAN.

I posti riservati ai tesserati CONI – FIGC – AIA saranno prenotabili (fino ad esaurimento dei posti disponibili) a partire dalle ore 16:00 di venerdì 4 dicembre 2026, previa registrazione attraverso la procedura presente al seguente link: https://sscnapoli.it/regolamento-accrediti-coni-figc-aia/.

INFORMAZIONI RELATIVE ALL’ACQUISTO DI TITOLI DIGITALI (CARICATI SU FIDELITY CARD).

Con il caricamento del titolo in modalità digitale sulla fidelity card, l’acquirente riceverà via mail (se acquistato sul Sito Sport.ticketone.it (si apre in una nuova scheda) o https://sscnapoli.ticketone.it/catalog (si apre in una nuova scheda) ), ovvero direttamente dal personale del punto vendita abilitato presso il quale sia stato eseguito l’acquisto, un tagliando/segnaposto.

Per accedere allo Stadio sarà indispensabile portare con sé la propria fidelity card, il tagliando/segnaposto e un documento di riconoscimento valido, che dovranno essere esibiti ad ogni richiesta del personale di controllo presente allo stadio.

Si precisa che il tagliando/segnaposto non costituisce, di per sé, titolo valido di accesso allo stadio.

Sarà sempre possibile stampare il tagliando/segnaposto dal link: https://sport.ticketone.it/post-order (si apre in una nuova scheda) .

L’accesso allo Stadio dovrà avvenire in maniera ordinata, nel rispetto delle istruzioni impartite dalla SSC Napoli tramite il proprio personale, al fine di evitare assembramenti.

Al termine della gara, al fine di non creare assembramenti, il deflusso sarà contingentato e regolato dal personale di sicurezza. Pertanto, si invita il pubblico a restare al proprio posto e attendere le indicazioni degli steward per l’uscita.

La non osservanza dei protocolli può comportare sanzioni da parte delle autorità competenti.

La titolarità di un titolo di accesso allo Stadio Maradona comporta automaticamente l’accettazione del Regolamento d’uso dello Stadio e del Codice di regolamentazione della cessione dei titoli di accesso alle manifestazioni calcistiche della SSC Napoli SpA (“Codice di Condotta”), entrambi consultabili sul sito ufficiale sscnapoli.it .

Il Codice di Condotta contempla tutte le condotte ritenute rilevanti ai fini dell’applicazione di eventuali sanzioni da parte della SSC Napoli, le varie tipologie di sanzioni nonché le relative procedure di applicazione.

La SSC Napoli ricorda ai propri tifosi di prendere visione e di attenersi scrupolosamente alle prescrizioni del Codice di condotta e del Regolamento d’uso dello Stadio.

Lo Stadio Maradona è dotato di un sistema di videosorveglianza all’avanguardia in grado di identificare gli autori delle violazioni del Regolamento d’uso dello Stadio e del Codice di Condotta.

La SSC Napoli condanna qualunque comportamento violento, anche verbale, e ogni condotta che direttamente o comportarti offesa, denigrazione o insulto per motivi di razza, colore, religione, lingua, sesso, nazionalità, origine etnica ovvero configuri propaganda ideologica vietata dalla legge o comunque inneggiante a comportamenti discriminatori o, più in generale, che la SSC Napoli ritenga non rappresentativi della tradizione e della propria identità sportiva.

Martin O’Neill has told Oliver Sorensen that it’s now time for him to deliver in a Celtic jersey.

Recent findings suggest that the Danish midfielder arrived in Glasgow with a massive reputation after coming in on a one-year loan from Parma. But in his seven appearances to date, the 24-year-old has failed to show why the Italian club paid Midtjylland £8.4million for his services a year ago.

With Mika Baur sidelined for up to ten weeks with an ankle injury, Sorensen is likely to be afforded further opportunities to show his worth. But with Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain, Luke McCowan and Joel van den Berg all showing up well in the weekend win over St Mirren, O’Neill has warned that Sorensen needs to do more if he’s to force his way into his side.

‘He has, by his own admission, found it difficult,’ stated the Celtic manager.

‘I think that he also arrived late as well, trying to get to know people, trying to get his position, trying to get up to speed with what we do. And whatever we do, I bet you it’ll be something really different to what he was doing at Parma.

It has been revealed that ‘But now it would be up to him. And, certainly, it will be up to him to try and do something as rapidly as possible, whether it’s in the next couple of weeks.

Danish midfielder Oliver Sorensen has been lesser spotted at Celtic this season.

Recent findings suggest that ‘His strength is picking the ball up deep and running and going with it. I think that Van den Berg can do that as well. But that was the idea with losing (Arne) Engels, we were trying to get a like-for-like replacement.

It has been revealed that ‘At this minute, he has found it difficult. But he’s willing and he wants to learn.’.

Celtic face Torreense on Thursday with the game being played in Leiria as the host club’s normal ground doesn’t meet UEFA stadium requirements.

After losing their first three Europa League games to Ferencvaros, Benfica and Celta Vigo, O’Neill’s men earned a lifeline in the competition when they defeated Besiktas last time out.

With ten points likely to be needed to secure progression to the play-off round, the Celtic manager feels it’s imperative that his side are on the seven-point mark after they take on Omonia on matchday six on December 10.

In a recent development, ‘We just want to try and do well,’ he stressed. ‘I mentioned after the Besiktas game that it gives you a chance.

Sorensen struggled along with the rest of his team-mates in a Europa League defeat at Benfica.

Sources indicate that ‘Because nobody’s made it after having lost the first three games. So, the next two matches are vital for us.

‘You’d have to think that we’d need to get four points in the two games to give ourselves a chance.

Sources indicate that ‘After that you’ve got two left over, a home game (Marseille), which will not be easy. And then the away match (Union Saint-Gilloise).

‘It would be nice to carry it into January and still have a chance.

Sources indicate that ‘We’ve taken enough criticism for not doing well enough in Europe and rightly so. It’s the aim of the football club, it’s what we’ve always said, and that’s been really disappointing.’.

Meanwhile, O’Neill believes Kieran Tierney is rediscovering the form which earned him a £25million move to Arsenal in 2019.

The full-back played the entirety of Scotland’s double-header with North Macedonia and Switzerland and lasted 71 minutes of the win over St Mirren – a game in which he claimed two assists.

O'Neill believes Kieran Tierney is close to the form that earned him a £25m move to Arsenal.

Recent findings suggest that delighted that the player appeared to be putting fitness concerns behind him, O’Neill said: ‘Kieran has done great for me. He’s been brilliant, he really has, and he’s getting fitter too.

According to recent reports, ‘He will be major for us in Europe again. You look at the Besiktas game. Our winning goal late on came from his shot when he was still getting high up the pitch.

‘Kieran has done so well for us and there are signs that he’s back to the Kieran Tierney who got a move to Arsenal.

‘He defends well, he creates goals and he comes up with some too. I genuinely couldn’t speak highly enough about him. He’s a great lad too, very popular in the dressing room.

According to recent reports, ‘Kieran can play as a centre-half, there’s no doubt about it. He competes better in the air than I ever thought he could. It was only when I came back to Celtic that I realised that.

It has been revealed that ‘He will battle in the air and he’s a reliable defender. If we are ever dropping into a back three, then it wouldn’t be a problem for him.’.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM.

It has been revealed that sono d'accordo, ci sta mancando in questo momento. Diamo la sensazione di voler giocare a calcio e di voler accarezzare il pallone, ma le gare si decidono dentro l'area. Negli ultimi metri non sono solo gli attaccanti, ma tutta la squadra: dobbiamo prendere più l'iniziativa e osare per creare di più. Nell'ultimo terzo ci arriviamo, ma poi succede troppo poco.

Affrontiamo la capolista, sono forti fisicamente e di qualità. Sono intensi, bravi nelle ripartenze e nelle riaggressioni, e giocano con spensieratezza. Per noi è difficile, dobbiamo cercare di fare punti. Faremo di tutto. Gattuso? Per me è difficile trovare le parole giuste... Mi ha protetto, mi ha fatto crescere, un fratello maggiore. E' un piacere ritrovarlo, lo abbraccerò forte.

According to recent reports, sappiamo che per i punti si avverte pesantezza e delusione, i primi delusi siamo noi. Tutti dobbiamo dare di più.

La difesa a quattro può essere una possibilità. Su Rodriguez non so ancora, mi confronto oggi con la società.

Recent findings suggest that loro sono intensi in tutti i reparti, serve una gara di carattere. Dobbiamo battagliare.

In a recent development, non so se è una coincidenza o se in quel gruppo ci fosse l'attitudine a fare l'allenatore. C'erano tante persone con un grande valore umano, mi hanno trasferito valori che ho fatto miei. Molti di loro li considero amici.

Industry observers note that lo vedo in crescendo, mi ha dato grandi sensazioni. Per noi una punta fisica come lui ci può fare comodo: nel calcio moderno, quando ti aggrediscono, serve appoggiarsi su una struttura come la sua. Mi auguro che cresca ancora.

Dobbiamo essere coscienti dei momenti della stagione. Abbiamo avuto risultati positivi cavalcando sull'entusiasmo, poi bisogna stare dentro a questi momenti. Voglio qualcosa in più per far girare la ruota. Ripeto: lavorare in certe piazza non è per tutti, noi dobbiamo di essere all'altezza della situazione senza piangersi addosso.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By WILL PICKWORTH, SPORTS REPORTER.

Published: 08:00 EST, 24 November 2026 | Updated: 14:15 EST, 24 November 2026.

There are few transfers that get West Ham supporters talking quite like the sale of an academy graduate.

Who can forget the uproar after Grady Diangana joined West Brom in 2020, when club captain Mark Noble released a public statement voicing his anger and disappointment at the move.

Noble’s thoughts were echoed by team-mates at the time, while supporters were similarly up in arms at the sale of the winger.

So, when Freddie Potts joined Club Brugge for £10million on the eve of the season to mark the controversial departure of another product of the proclaimed Academy of Football, you can imagine the reaction.

According to recent reports, potts represented more than a graduate. A boyhood West Ham fan whose dad Steve is a club legend and still serves as a first-team coach, he joined the academy aged six. His brother Dan also came through the ranks.

The midfielder had just enjoyed a breakthrough campaign despite West Ham’s relegation, and many felt he was the perfect player to build their Championship promotion push around.

Freddie Potts is shining in Belgium with Club Brugge after joining from West Ham in the summer.

Potts joined the Hammers academy aged six and enjoyed a breakthrough year last season.

Hammers favourites Kevin Nolan and Tony Cottee weighed in with their disapproval at his sale, while celebrity fan Ray Winstone expressed his shock and anger live on talkSPORT.

Industry observers note that ‘Of course you see it (the division about the move) on social media,’ Potts tells Daily Mail Sport. ‘Every player does. But even though last season was tough I always felt I had a connection with the West Ham fans.

It has been revealed that ‘No matter if I played well or bad I always felt I understood what it meant to play for West Ham. It's a great club with great fans and people. In the end, I had to do what was best for me. I wanted to play this season, and I felt like this was the best place to do that.’.

Potts, 22 at the time of his exit, admits it was extremely tough and emotional for him and his family to leave a club he had been at for 16 years.

But, during pre-season he became aware he wasn’t likely to play as much as he wanted to under Nuno Espirito Santo.

Industry observers note that ‘In the end it’s the manager’s decision,’ Potts claims. ‘I wasn’t getting the minutes I wanted. The feeling was that I wasn’t guaranteed to be in the plans as much as Club Brugge were promising me, so I thought it was best for me to move.

‘It was very hard. West Ham have been my club my whole life and I have a lot of love for West Ham. But I had to take into account what was best for my career and I’m loving it at Brugge. It’s a really exciting place full of great people and a great manager.’.

Potts had multiple options in the summer, including Premier League interest, yet the chance to play in the Champions League and compete for titles with Brugge attracted him.

Their record of developing young players and a talented squad that includes the likes of Carlos Forbs and Nicolo Tresoldi was equally compelling, and the midfielder hasn't looked back.

Potts started Brugge’s first 10 league games, missing their final one before the international break due to suspension. He returned at the weekend as they thrashed Mechelen 5-1. Ivan Leko’s side are one point adrift of Union Saint-Gilloise at the top of the Belgian Pro League, and they have also impressed in the Champions League.

In Europe, Brugge have beaten Inter Milan, PSV and Lens on their way to nine points from 12, only narrowly losing 3-2 to Aston Villa. Potts has started each match, including their memorable 4-3 win against Inter at the San Siro, and they host Liverpool on Wednesday.

Industry observers note that ‘It's a really good group of lads,’ he states. ‘Everyone speaks English as well which helps me. It's a good team and we're happy playing with each other.’.

It has been revealed that he is clearly enjoying life and is just the fifth English player in history to play for the club. Potts did take time to settle though, and admits he initially suffered from homesickness.

Industry observers note that ‘I found it difficult because East London and Essex have been my home for my whole life,’ he says. ‘West Ham was my life. It was tough in terms of moving into a new language and everything but you get used to it and I’m really enjoying it here. It’ll be strange going back home to England.'.

Potts has been a regular and has had a key role in Brugge's impressive early exploits in Europe.

Brugge have beaten PSV, Lens and Inter Milan, and they take on Liverpool this Wednesday.

In a recent development, potts’ family have popped over to see him and he has enjoyed exploring his new surroundings. He is yet to learn the local language and scolds himself for being lazy for relying on English, although he has picked up little bits of Flemish.

He has immersed himself in the culture too, and reveals he has tried the world-famous Belgian fries and a few local beers, albeit only when he has enough time to recover between games.

Despite his newly introduced life in Europe, Potts remains a West Ham fan and tries to watch them on TV every week.

He has been surprised by their struggles on their return to the Championship for the first time in 14 years, with Nuno paying the price by losing his job. Former Hammers midfielder Scott Parker has since taken the reins.

‘I still think they're playing well,’ Potts says. ‘They've got a great team and Scott Parker is a really good manager. You get ups and downs but I still 100 per cent think West Ham will get promoted this year.'.

Potts’ stay in the Hammers first team may have been brief, yet there were still plenty of highs, not least a storming performance on his first Premier League start. That came in a win over Newcastle last November in the Hammers’ first home victory of the season. He was also coached by his dad, an experience he jokes had positives and negatives.

He left West Ham after realising he was unlikely to be first choice under Nuno Espirito Santo.

Potts is a boyhood West Ham fan and is fully expecting them to get promoted this season.

Industry observers note that attention now turns to Brugge’s clash against Liverpool. It promises to be a tricky challenge for Andoni Iraola’s side against a team who are determined to prove themselves on the European stage.

The two teams are level on points in the league phase, and Potts is keen for his side to take another scalp.

Industry observers note that ‘I don't think there's much difference in the way we've been performing in the Champions League,’ Potts concludes. ‘It'll be difficult for them to come to our place as well.

‘They're a great team, but we're going to approach it like we have with every Champions League game. We've gone away and beaten Milan, we've beaten PSV away. These are top teams.

‘Results like that give you a boost of how far you can go. You don't want to look too far ahead but every game in this competition is a chance to show everyone what you can do.

‘Liverpool will be a tough game but we've proved it against top teams before and we're going in thinking that we can do it again.’.

Alisson’s brilliance takes the breath away to show way forward for Liverpool

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Andoni Iraola spun on his heels, turned his back to the action and began to bite his nails. Managers often envisage the worst outcome when the clock ticks down, and here, in the 93rd minute, Bournemouth had a corner.

According to recent reports, he needn’t have worried. As the set-piece was swung in, Alisson Becker moved powerfully off his line and plucked the ball from the air, a catch that essentially confirmed Liverpool would leave Dorset with three points. It was a catch, too, that put the gloss on another impeccable personal afternoon.

Industry observers note that when Iraola took charge at Anfield, one question he had to answer – given Bournemouth had conceded 167 goals in his three years in charge – was whether he could make Liverpool defensively resilient. This dour 1-0 success, though, proves he is taking them in the right direction: he is the first Liverpool manager since Joe Fagan in 1983 to start with five unbeaten league games.

Alexander Isak might have scored the goal that leaves Bournemouth winless in the Premier League but this success owed everything to Alisson’s enduring brilliance – a comment that also applies to Virgil van Dijk – the enormous promise of Jérémy Jacquet and the grit of Ronaldo Araújo.

You go to top level football matches hoping to see something that will take your breath away and how Alisson did that in the 17th minute with a reflex save from an Evanilson backheel, the shape of his body resembling a fielder in the slips diving to prevent a boundary.

Sources indicate that it proved to be the foundation stone from which Liverpool were able to build and inflict Bournemouth’s first home defeat since January. There are plenty of [valid] questions to ask of Liverpool’s attack at present but, defensively, it is starting to come together.

Recent findings suggest that “It was a really good fight,” Alisson said, in that self-effacing way of his. “But we have to improve a lot – on the ball and sometimes off the ball as well but we improved in the second half. We adapted to the opponent and that’s what we are doing.”.

Any manager with a well-drilled defence stands a chance of improving and that is what Liverpool are doing. Only four weeks ago the discussion was about how easy it was for teams to play through their middle – remember that chaotic afternoon at Newcastle to start? – but that is changing swiftly.

Industry observers note that since Iraola replaced Jeremie Frimpong with Araújo at right-back, three consecutive Premier League clean sheets have followed. Araújo, the Uruguayan on loan from Barcelona, revels in doing the dirty work while Jacquet, the £60m signing from Rennes, oozes quality.

“He’s [Jacquet] very young and adapted really well to the Premier League,” Iraola said. “The first games, he was physically feeling the change of rhythm and I had to sub him. This was a step forward. He looked solid until the end. He’s in a good place physically and I hope he can continue his development.”.

Sources indicate that don’t confuse positivity about one aspect of the team as being a guide to its collective health. There was always a chance this contest would become a cagey affair and, Evanilson’s chance aside, the opening 45 minutes were as flat as you could imagine.

Iraola again played his three £100m+ signings but Bradley Barcola is still adjusting to the physicality of English football and Florian Wirtz is still finding it difficult to impose himself on a game; patience with the German will not be infinite.

He would do worse than to look at Isak, who is now on a run of four goals in four league games and is influencing games in the manner Liverpool envisaged when they broke the British transfer record to sign him last August.

Recent findings suggest that isak had an unusual afternoon. His only shot in the first half almost took out some low-flying pigeons, a cross early in the second half was sliced so badly that the weekend hackers on the nearby Queens Park golf course would have felt a flood of sympathy but then he got his third opening.

Cody Gakpo, who could have been in Manchester City blue had the cards played out differently earlier this month, wriggled down the right flank and squeezed in a cross that Isak seized upon and turned in from six yards. Liverpool never looked back.

Alexander Isak grabs his fourth Premier League goal of the season! 🔴 pic.twitter.com/5ehwhl1it4.

“A striker’s job is like this,” Iraola remarked, who badgered Isak persistently to press Bournemouth’s defence. “He had a couple of crosses that he did not hit properly or control. He has to help us to be closer to the box, to play in the opposition’s half and have more meaningful possession. And then if the team is playing there, he will receive rewards in terms of goals.”.

One, ultimately, was enough to see off Bournemouth, whose start to the campaign is something of a riddle. They shouldn’t be anywhere near the relegation places but that is the reality and Thursday’s historic Europa League win in Real Sociedad couldn’t mask the home crowd’s frustration.

“Our attitude and effort is good,” head coach Marco Rose stated. “But, at this level, small things and little details decide games.”.

Speaking to Sky Sports after the match, Iraola mentioned: “I’m obviously happy with the result because I know this is a difficult place to come, very difficult place to get three points. And we could see it, especially in the beginning of the game. In the first 20 minutes we weren’t at the level [required] and it cost us. We finished the first half better and in the second half we played better, but that beginning of the game has surprised us, not surprised us [because] we knew where we were coming but it [was] difficult for us.”.

Jeremy Jacquet has made the kind of quietly authoritative start to his Liverpool career that indicated why there was such excitement in February within the club when they completed his deal. So much focus on so many players but Jacquet has never been anything other 7.5/8 out of 10.

Industry observers note that "Let's go! One of many!" Virgil van Dijk giving Jérémy Jacquet his POTM award after Liverpool's 1-0 win at Bournemouth ⭐️ pic.twitter.com/6xWvjmrF8Y.

"That's a significant moment to me to play with Virgil!" 🫡Jérémy Jacquet after Liverpool's 1-0 win at Bournemouth! pic.twitter.com/UsTimGME39.

Sources indicate that cody Gakpo has been Liverpool’s stand-out forward this term and he was at the heart of Isak’s goal this afternoon. Speaking about the job the Dutchman is doing to fill the void left by Mohamed Salah on the right flank, Ashley Young stated on Sky Sports: “Players have to step up when you lose significant players and you get the opportunities. I think Cody Gakpo is doing that. He’s a bit fortunate [in the build-up to Liverpool’s goal] but you create your own luck. He gets the ball down the line, that’s what you want to do and he puts the ball in the box. That’s what Isak’s waiting for.”.

Fair play to anyone who retained Brobbey in their Fantasy Football teams this week...

Andoni Iraola returns to Bournemouth this weekend knowing what to expect from players he understands so well. Sadly, I do not mean Liverpool’s.

Having built his reputation creating a hard-working, well-drilled team rich in potential, Iraola is responsible for infusing those same characteristics into the most expensively assembled squad in Liverpool history.

According to recent reports, his first six games demonstrate it is no quick fix. The Basque coach is the first Liverpool appointment to work with more than £700m of recent signings while being entitled to feel he has been dealt a bad hand.

In a recent development, everything Iraola has said and done so far screams that he is searching for the right blend in his starting XI while having to eradicate negative traits, with and without the ball. It was telling that the excellent performance of his youngsters against Tottenham Hotspur in midweek offered the clearest hint of Iraola’s vision than anything we have seen with all the high-priced stars on the pitch.

It has been revealed that there is a reason the Kop stood to acclaim the energy and application of youngsters Lewis Koumas, James McConnell and Trey Nyoni – and why Iraola keeps name-checking them. Iraola is indebted to them for issuing a reminder of the non-negotiables that come with being a Liverpool footballer; regardless of price tag and reputation, leaving everything on the pitch is compulsory. It is a concern that so many of the renowned players need to hear that message.

Jurgen Klopp named Florian Wirtz in his first squad as Germany manager and has remarked that fans must refrain from expecting “special moments” from the Liverpool playmaker as a matter of course.

Of Wirtz, he mentioned: “I think he’s the player who covered the most ground at Liverpool this season, so the willingness is absolutely there.

“We have to move away from the idea that we need to see special moments from him. He is there to help us as a team. We have to make sure that Flo feels comfortable with us.”.

Wirtz has delivered seven goals and 11 assists in his 54 Liverpool appearances.

Sources indicate that adam Smith, 35, played for Iraola 81 times and he admitted his former manager’s visit to the Vitality will be a sentimental affair. He remarked: “It’s going to be an emotional day for everyone I think, [for] our ex-manager and some of our players that have played under him, but we’ll be up for the game for sure.”.

According to recent reports, good afternoon and welcome to our live coverage of the Premier League match between Liverpool and Bournemouth as Andoni Iraola returns to the Vitality Stadium for the first time since his big move up north. The Basque propelled Bournemouth to latest heights, guiding the club into Europe and his successor, Marco Rose, ensured they made a winning start to life on the Continent by defeating Real Sociedad in midweek.

Previewing Iraola’s Vitality Stadium return, Craig Beazley, host and creator of the Up The Cherries In All Departments podcast, said: “We’ve now got the Andoni Iraola return … Andoni is very much a legend really, there should be a statue of Sir Eddie Howe and Sir Andoni Iraola [outside the ground] as well.”.

Across three seasons, Iraola guided Bournemouth to 12th, ninth and sixth in the Premier League, winning 47 of his 127 matches in charge (37 per cent).

Liverpool are still acclimatising to his exacting style of play and their results suggest as much. They are 10th in the table having drawn three and won one, impressing in flashes but struggling to maintain consistently productive final-third patterns and pressing structures. Deploying Ronald Araújo at right-back has proved effective, though, with Liverpool conceding just two goals in their last four matches.

Sources indicate that the Cherries are searching for their first Premier League win of the season and have retained the 4-2-3-1 shape from the Iraola days, with Rose preferring a similarly vertical attacking strategy. They continue to leverage their strengths in transitions and in wide areas as Adrien Truffert rains in crosses for any one of Bournemouth’s exuberant frontline to pounce on.

Elsewhere, Manchester City welcome Sunderland, who also secured a Europa League win during the week, to the Etihad while in-form Leeds United host Crystal Palace knowing a win would lift them into the top four.

Immagini di terminare la tua carriera al Napoli? Per te è un sogno, un pensiero, ci pensi? "Sì, sarebbe bello, però non sappiamo quanto tempo giocherò. Tu parli molto bene la lingua italiana, ormai sei anche un napoletano doc. Con il napoletano come va? Hai imparato qualcosa? “Il napoletano è un po’ difficile, però capisco quando parlano i napoletani tra di loro. Sì, dico una parola, ma queste che sanno più o meno tutti: fratm’”.

Con i tuoi compagni il napoletano va bene? C’è qualcuno, per esempio McTominay o Hojlund, che sa già qualcosina? “Non ho sentito parlare tanto, perché loro non parlano tanto italiano, però non ho sentito parole napoletane, tranne queste che sono più semplici”.

The brain keeps the score: how trauma leaves molecular scars in cells

📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (795 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nature

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Researchers examined DNA methylation in brain regions, including the amygdala and hippocampus, which are parts of the limbic system shown here.Credit: K H Fung/Science Photo Library.
  • A post-mortem analysis of more than 300 people is offering newly introduced insights into how trauma chemically alters the brain.
  • The study, published in Cell Reports on 20 November1, identifies molecular changes to DNA inside the brain cells of people with post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) and depression.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Researchers examined DNA methylation in brain regions, including the amygdala and hippocampus, which are parts of the limbic system shown here.Credit: K H Fung/Science Photo Library.

A post-mortem analysis of more than 300 people is offering newly introduced insights into how trauma chemically alters the brain.

The study, published in Cell Reports on 20 November1, identifies molecular changes to DNA inside the brain cells of people with post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) and depression. These include ‘epigenetic marks’ — chemical tags added to DNA as a result of environmental influences, including stress and trauma. Epigenetic marks can affect how genes work, but do not alter DNA sequences.

The analysis “gives the most comprehensive look at cell type differences” in brain regions following PTSD diagnosis, claims Alicia Smith, who studies the epigenetics of PTSD at Emory University in Atlanta, Georgia.

Sources indicate that PTSD can develop after experiencing a traumatic event, causing symptoms such as flashbacks, anxiety and emotional distress. Understanding its epigenetic consequences helps researchers to track how trauma can alter gene regulation, and perhaps explain why some people experience symptoms and respond to treatment differently.

The study analysed postmortem brain tissues and medical records donated by 101 people who were diagnosed with PTSD, 101 people with depression and 100 control participants who did not have a mental-health condition. The researchers examined DNA methylation in brain cells — an epigenetic mechanism in which methyl groups are added to or removed from DNA sequences.

Many previous studies of epigenetic marks linked to PTSD have used samples of DNA from blood2 or saliva3. “What we really want to understand is what’s going on in the brain,” indicates study co-author Frances Champagne, a behavioural epigeneticist at the University of Texas at Austin.

Champagne and her colleagues examined DNA methylation across more than 850,000 genomic regions in cells taken from three parts of the brain: the amygdala, hippocampus and prefrontal cortex, which are involved in emotion processing, memory and cognitive control, respectively.

According to recent reports, the study found distinct methylation patterns in four DNA regions in the prefrontal cortex when comparing the PTSD group with the control group, but none in the amygdala or the hippocampus. One gene affected by these unique DNA methylations had not been previously linked to PTSD, but has a key role in memory.

Recent findings suggest that the researchers also identified differences at the cellular level. Compared with the control group, the amygdala in people with PTSD had significantly reduced levels of oligodendrocytes — cells that create a protective, insulating sheath around the connections between neurons and facilitate communication between them.

How I explore trauma through ‘cinematic neuroscience’.

How I explore trauma through ‘cinematic neuroscience’.

The amygdala is central to fear responses. “That decrease in oligodendrocytes that we see in PTSD seems to be linked to, particularly, exposure to adult trauma,” notes Champagne. Oligodendrocytes were reduced across all three brain regions in 58 people who had experienced trauma as adults, regardless of whether or not they were diagnosed with a disorder. The researchers did not observe the same pattern in 97 donors who experienced childhood trauma.

Entrambe le parti devono impegnarsi affinché ci sia un finale degno della sua carriera. 📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By BOBBY MANZI, FOOTBALL REPORTER.

Published: 09:30 EST, 24 November 2026 | Updated: 14:47 EST, 24 November 2026.

Senegal have been reinstated as Africa Cup of Nations winners after succeeding with an appeal to the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS), ten months after they beat Morocco in Rabat.

The ruling follows a controversial final in which Senegal initially won 1-0 after extra time, only for the result to be overturned following an appeal to Confederation of African Football (CAF) by the Moroccan Football Federation.

Two months after the final, the CAF appeal board ruled that Senegal had forfeited the match because their players had walked off the pitch in protest over a controversial penalty decision.

Morocco were subsequently awarded a 3-0 victory and the title. Despite that, Senegal refused to hand the trophy over.

That decision was based on Articles 82 and 84 of the AFCON regulations, which state that leaving the pitch constitutes a forfeit.

However, following an appeal to CAS, Senegal have been reinstalled as champions, with the court ruling that FIFA's law that the referee’s decision is final takes precedence over the competition regulations.

Therefore, because the officials did not enforce the competition regulations at the time, there were no grounds to overturn the result.

The Moroccan FA, though, have not given up and have vowed to take the matter beyond CAS after questioning the integrity of panelist Ulrich Haas.

The Court of Arbitration for Sport has restored Senegal as Africa Cup of Nations winners after they were successful in their appeal.

Morocco were awarded a 3-0 victory two months after the final, after it was ruled Senegal had forfeited the match by walking off the pitch in protest over a late penalty decision.

Senegal fans clashed with security in Rabat after the controversial penalty decision.

Ruling in favour of Senegal on Tuesday, CAS said: 'In the Panel’s view, there is no doubt that the effects of the Referee’s decision were limited to the pitch.

'As such, the Panel considers that the Referee’s decision was covered by the "field of play" doctrine.

'Since Articles 82 and 84 of the AFCON Regulations are intended solely to determine the outcome of a match when a team’s conduct leads the referee to call off the game permanently, they are therefore not applicable in this case.'.

Industry observers note that A statement from the Moroccan FA later added: 'We take note of the decision of the Court of Arbitration for Sport regarding the appeal filed by the Senegalese Football Federation against the decision of the CAF Appeals Committee, relating to the final match of the 2025 Africa Cup of Nations. In this context, the Royal Moroccan Football Federation expresses its surprise and protest at the failure to take into account its demand to arrange the necessary legal consequences for practices that would compromise the integrity and credibility of the arbitration procedure, especially what has been confirmed regarding communication between the German referee Ulrich Haas (who sat on the CAS panel) and the president of the Senegalese Football Federation, 48 hours before the decision was issued.

'The Royal Moroccan Football Federation also notes that the decision did not take into account the approach recently adopted by both the International Football Association Board (IFAB) and FIFA, regarding players leaving the field of play without the referee’s permission, and the resulting disciplinary responsibilities and penalties.

'Accordingly, the Royal Moroccan Football Federation confirms its intention to pursue all available legal avenues to appeal the decision of the Court of Arbitration for Sport.'.

The chaos was triggered by events at the end of normal time, when referee Jean Jacques Ndala awarded Morocco a contentious penalty in the 98th minute after being called to the monitor by the video assistant referee to review El Hadji Malick Diouf’s challenge on Brahim Diaz.

The decision came just minutes after Senegal had seen a goal ruled out.

Furious with the penalty decision, Senegal manager Pape Thiaw instructed his players to leave the pitch in protest.

After a 17-minute delay, the team eventually returned, with former Liverpool forward Sadio Mane earning praise for remaining on the pitch and encouraging his teammates to continue.

In the dramatic aftermath, Real Madrid forward Brahim Diaz saw his Panenka penalty stopped by Senegal goalkeeper Edouard Mendy, before Ndala brought normal time to an end.

Senegal went on to score early in extra time, which has now led to a second title in the past three editions of the tournament with their 1-0 victory eventually confirmed in the courtroom.
