Il tecnico dell'Aston Villa Unai Emery ha parlato in conferenza stampa del momento della sua squadra partendo dal ko di Istanbul contro il Galatasaray: "Ovviamente, in Champions League la situazione è un po' diversa; arriviamo da due sconfitte in trasferta, contro Barcellona e Galatasaray, che sono state partite piuttosto differenti tra loro. Ma credo, e ne sono fiducioso, nel modo in cui stiamo lavorando, nei progressi che stiamo compiendo e nell'importanza di avere, a volte, un po' di pazienza.

Certo, la Premier League non aspetta nessuno, ma a volte è necessario avere pazienza, continuare a lavorare e cercare di fare un passo avanti, sia a livello collettivo che individuale, avendo ben chiaro che questa è la strada che vogliamo intraprendere. Stiamo costruendo la nostra struttura, cercando di consolidare il nostro stile di gioco: vogliamo sentirci a nostro agio nel mantenere il possesso palla, cercando di dominare il campo e di gestire il pallone con sicurezza.

Ora, partendo da questa base solida, dobbiamo cercare di ottenere qualcosa in più in attacco. A livello individuale, serve più incisività nel dribbling e negli inserimenti alle spalle della difesa; è fondamentale mantenere i collegamenti tra centrocampisti, difensori centrali, attaccanti ed esterni, affinché i movimenti avvengano nei momenti giusti: questo è chiaramente un aspetto su cui dobbiamo migliorare".

In casa Napoli si lavora al mercato e la priorità è regalare ad Allegri un vice-Hojlund, un calciatore che possa dare ricambio in maniera consistente al danese e allo stesso tempo eventualmente giocare insieme.

It has been revealed that il club sembra intenzionato a puntare sull’attaccante campano Sebastiano Esposito, attualmente in prestito al Sassuolo, ma di proprietà del Cagliari. Il calciatore è il profilo adatto, per caratteristiche e cifre, per sostituire Lorenzo Lucca, sempre più ai margini e ormai giocatore che verrà ceduto a gennaio. La trattativa tra le parti è già cominciata e il Napoli sembra intenzionato a sferrare a gennaio l’attacco decisivo per Esposito.

Come riporta Il Mattino il Napoli è in pole per Sebastiano Esposito, nelle ultime settimane l’agente del giocatore Giuffredi ha incontrato Giovanni Manna e la trattativa è stata ormai già preimpostata. Il presidente azzurro De Laurentiis vuole riportare l’attaccante in Campania e il giocatore può arrivare a costi piuttosto contenuti per un profilo da Nazionale.

According to recent reports, il Sassuolo può riscattare Esposito per 10 milioni di euro circa e il Napoli potrebbe chiudere la trattativa a circa 14-15 milioni di euro, una trattativa che il Napoli potrebbe realizzare anche in prestito con obbligo di riscatto a fine anno. Le parti ragionano sul da farsi, ma sarà Esposito il nuovo attaccante per gennaio.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, sheffield United cut ties with the striker following their last promotion to the Premier League. SUFC decided not to hand him a contract extension at Bramall Lane and he subsequently became a free agent.

According to recent reports, sharp, now 40, had three separate spells as a player at Bramall Lane. He announced his retirement in October but has since featured in non-league for AFC Rushden & Diamonds.

According to recent reports, he has opened up about his departure from his boyhood club three-and-a-half years ago on Sky Sports’ Essential EFL Podcast: “I had a chance about three or four years before (to leave), Colorado Rapids were potentially going to take me but it wasn’t the right time. I didn’t leave Sheffield United. Sheffield United didn’t offer me a fresh contract which was so disappointing for me because I got told by the owners and by the manager three times that I was going to get another year. I got told on the day of the parade that I wasn’t going to get it which absolutely ruined the day for me.

“I was distraught. I was going to retire at 37, that was me thinking ‘do you know what, I’ve had such a good career and I can’t see myself playing for another team’. I wanted to end at Sheffield United but I was out of contract for the first time in my career and (then) LA Galaxy came calling.”.

Sharp rose up through Sheffield United’s academy as a youngster and was a regular for them at various different youth levels. He went on to play twice for SUFC’s first-team before leaving for Scunthorpe United in 2005.

Industry observers note that the Blades re-signed him two years later and he scored 13 goals in 64 matches before embarking on spells at Doncaster Rovers, Southampton, Nottingham Forest, Reading and Leeds United. Chris Wilder lured him back to his hometown team for a third time when they were in League One in 2015.

Sharp helped Sheffield United rise from the third tier to the Premier League and found the net on 116 occasions in 311 outings. However, his former club didn’t offer him fresh terms under Paul Heckingbottom and he subsequently became available.

It has been revealed that as he has now alluded to, he considered hanging up his boots before LA Galaxy came calling. His stint in America was brief though and he later returned with Hull City before Doncaster Rovers brought him back.

Recent findings suggest that sharp will go down as one of Sheffield United’s greatest ever strikers. He is a legend at SUFC and it wouldn’t be a surprise to see him go back there in some capacity down the line.

The Blades are presently looking to claw themselves out of the EFL and back into the top flight if possible. They drew 1-1 at home against Southampton on Tuesday night with midfielder Sydie Peck scoring a late equaliser.

In a recent development, wilder‘s side are sat in 9th place in the table after 17 fixtures and they are only one place outside the play-offs. They are one point behind Swansea City in 8th and could rise into the top eight this weekend if results go their way.

Sheffield United face a tricky away trip down to QPR on Saturday. Their upcoming opponents are positioned in 7th.

Published: 18:37 EST, 24 November 2026 | Updated: 18:42 EST, 24 November 2026.

Derek McInnes last night hit out at his dozy Rangers side for switching off in the latter stages of a hard-fought 3-2 home win over Aberdeen and warned them they will be made to pay over the course of the season if they carry on being so naive.

Goals from Ryan Naderi, Djeidi Gassama and Raskin in the first ten minutes of the second half put the Ibrox outfit in total command after Brad Lyons had put the visitors a goal up at the break.

However, Findlay Marshall made it a nervy finish for Rangers after scoring for the Dons on 58 minutes and it took a brilliant save from keeper Ivor Pandur to deny Nicky Devlin before Rangers saw it out to take their unbeaten run to 14 games and close the gap on Celtic at the head of the Premiership to just one point.

‘I am relieved to win,’ said manager McInnes, who made three changes and altered the shape at the interval. ‘I thought we only played with the intelligence, speed and intensity for about 20 minutes and, in that period, showed how good we can be.

‘But we put the game at risk. We lost a cheap goal and weren’t aggressive enough. We lost two goals, really, from set-plays.

‘At 3-1 up against a team as game as Aberdeen were — and they were really good value — our naivety for the second goal is beyond me.

Rangers boss Derek McInnes was relieved to win but urges his side to keep focused.

Nicolas Raskin slots home the third goal for Rangers in their thrilling 3-2 win over Aberdeen.

‘I am not sure it was a free-kick in the first place, but we turn our backs. It is almost as if we are in a daydream and we allow them to manipulate the ball. Great finish from wee Findlay Marshall, but we put ourselves in the mire there by just knocking off.

It has been revealed that ‘We were so naive at times in the game. We scored good goals at good times but I still think Aberdeen will be disappointed not to get something.

It has been revealed that ‘We should have stayed in charge of the game and the second goal we lose allows Aberdeen to keep going with a bit of oxygen and carry a threat. I am disappointed with the lack of control in the game and I am not really happy with a lot of what we saw.

‘That has to change because we will not always be able to outscore the opposition.

‘We hit Aberdeen like a train in the second half and they found themselves 3-1 down because of the quality and intelligence of our play. For whatever reason, we then started playing back the way again. We played more passbacks to my goalkeeper than I can remember in a long time.

Recent findings suggest that ‘We need to play forward and show more control in the game. I am looking for better from my team.’.

Raskin, meanwhile, has urged his Rangers team-mates to blast themselves to the top of the table on Saturday night and really pile the pressure on arch-rivals Celtic.

The Light Blues play host to third-placed Falkirk on Saturday afternoon with Celtic going to Hearts the following day and the Belgian midfielder wants to make sure they don’t let the defending champions off the hook the way they have in previous years.

‘We need to keep it going,’ mentioned Raskin. ‘In recent years, we have not been able to put enough pressure on the other team and now we are doing it, so that is good.

‘We will see how everybody reacts after next Saturday.’.

Djeidi Gassama scored to complete a stunning turaround for Rangers early in the second half.

Raskin has also revealed it took a stern half-time team talk from manager McInnes along with those substitutions to spark his side into life after a dreadful first-half performance.

‘I think we made the game hard for ourselves in the first half,’ noted the Belgian. ‘The manager had an honest discussion in the dressing room and we came back and scored two early goals, which helped. But we weren’t focused enough after the third goal and conceded to make it even harder.

‘We showed character again. The manager stated what a manager has to say when you are losing, playing badly, you are 1-0 down and you have to win the game.’.

Aberdeen boss Mario Frick left Ibrox feeling his side had missed a real opportunity.

‘I am disappointed with the five or six minutes after half-time. That hurts,’ he remarked.

‘We saw a good performance, Rangers were beatable tonight.

In a recent development, ‘We need more time. We have to improve. We have to talk about those ten minutes. After 3-1 down, we came back and we believed in ourselves. We deserved an equaliser.’.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Thomas Tuchel has never been inclined to place much faith in the most famous right-back at his disposal, Trent Alexander-Arnold, once of Liverpool, now of Real Madrid, and – back in an England shirt – still capable of changing games in the blink of an eye.

In a recent development, england always looked likely to defeat a beleaguered Czech Republic team down to 10 men with just 25 minutes played, but it still required one man to conjure the moment of inspiration in this Nations League tie. This was the first cap in 15 months for the right-back now known simply as “Trent” in an England shirt – as well as his Real Madrid jersey – rather than the six syllables of his surname. With the game level at half-time, two minutes into the upcoming half, he twice won the ball before landing a cross on the head of Anthony Gordon for the first goal.

TRENT ➡️ GORDON ⚽️🔥Anthony Gordon can't stop scoring for England, 3 goals in his last 3 games for England 🏴󠁧󠁢󠁥󠁮󠁧󠁿#ITVFootball | @England pic.twitter.com/xmqPIULJ24.

Will the Alexander-Arnold with England experiment survive? One feels that Tuchel will need a little more to convince him to abandon whatever reservations he has about the Liverpudlian. A week short of his 28th birthday, Alexander-Arnold was winning just his 35th cap. His Real Madrid team-mate Jude Bellingham, a second-half substitute, was earning his 58th cap less than two months after his 23rd birthday. Bellingham was on as captain in place of the man he replaced, Harry Kane, scorer of England’s second. Bellingham’s international career has taken a much less rocky path than that of his Real team-mate.

Industry observers note that having missed the World Cup finals this summer, and had little good fortune around previous tournaments, one wonders if Euro 2028 might be the watershed moment for Alexander-Arnold. Either way, against opponents who sit back, he is lethal when it is time for the significant delivery. Alexander-Arnold may not have the breadth of England experience that some of his peers have accumulated, but he does have plenty of experience of big games.

Recent findings suggest that “I make that run time and time again,” Gordon noted of his anticipation of the Alexander-Arnold cross, “but only a set number of players have that ability, that technique and the bravery to risk a mistake to play that pass. And that’s why I have been dying to play with him [Alexander-Arnold]. He’s been on his own journey but has trained really well this week. He should have played more. Sorry – he would have loved to have played more.”.

It has been revealed that A Freudian slip from the Barcelona winger, another Liverpudlian in Spain, who himself has barely put a foot wrong for England of late. He has three goals in three games for England, including the World Cup semi-final against Argentina. This was an England team that Tuchel fine-tuned, first to give a rest to Bellingham and in other quarters, too. Lewis Hall started at left-back. Trevoh Chalobah won his third England cap at centre-back. Alex Scott, of Bournemouth, was given his debut off the bench in the second half and Rio Ngumoha won the second cap of his England career, just one month after his 18th birthday.

It has been revealed that as for Kane, his 87th goal for England now puts him within two goals of Robert Lewandowski, among four greats in the seven ahead of Kane on the all-time international goalscorers’ list. By the end of this international break the England captain should have equalled Peter Shilton’s record 125 caps. It has been an astonishing career even if it ends tomorrow. Following the missed penalty against Spain, Kane was again the man in the right place at the right time when Morgan Rogers’s shot was blocked in the second half.

In a recent development, “Strange to get an early red card,” Tuchel noted. “Not the best for the team and spectators. Sulc, the Czech player of the year in 2025, had mistimed a tackle on Elliot Anderson, which on a VAR review, the Turkish referee Umut Meler decided was worthy of an upgrade from yellow to red. Thomas Tuchel has backed Jude Bellingham as a future England captain after giving him the armband in the victory over the Czech Republic.

In the absence of Declan Rice, who was vice-captain at the World Cup, Bellingham assumed the role when he came on for Harry Kane, who is now in his 10th season as England captain and also scored in the 2-0 win in Prague.

Tuchel, who needs to check on Bellingham ahead of Saturday’s game against Croatia after a “niggle,” has praised the midfielder’s attitude during the extended international break one year after he was back from an injury but left out of the squad.

“If you are the captain at the end of these matches, you can be the permanent captain,” Tuchel mentioned when asked whether Bellingham could eventually lead the team. “He was the captain against Newly introduced Zealand before the World Cup. It is always a reward and always an honour.

According to recent reports, “I think he loves to be with us at the moment. That’s what I feel, and we had this small talk today about his role. We felt in our hearts or our stomachs to say ‘let’s go again, let’s start again’ and also our heads told us maybe 30 minutes is enough for this match because he hasn’t played in this quick turnaround through this season. He has done it before, but not in the season, so we didn’t want to be the first ones to try that.

In a recent development, “But even in this little encounter, you can see that he’s confident and happy to help from the bench. So it’s a reward. It’s good. He had a little niggle at the end of the match, so hopefully it’s nothing serious, and he’s available for Croatia.”.

Nico O’Reilly is a doubt for the Croatia match in Rijeka and there are also concerns over Ezri Konsa, who was on the bench but not fit enough to play.

The Professional Footballers’ Association has leapt to Cole Palmer’s defence following his withdrawal from the England squad.

The union’s CEO,  Maheta Molango, remarked the Chelsea forward is a victim of a “sick” system that is demanding too much from players physically.

“When England see five players who need to withdraw when the single most proud moment a player has is to be called up for the national team, you just ask yourself, what’s wrong about the industry?” Molango noted at the Fifpro performance summit in London.

“You see people like Cole Palmer, someone who would have played four consecutive summers in a row had he gone to the World Cup, and you wonder why is he missing?”He’s missing because he’s a victim of the calendar and that’s something that needs to absolutely trigger the alarm bells.”.

Man City used ‘sham’ sponsorships in £830m cheating scheme.

Manchester City arranged “sham” sponsorships in a near-£1bn plot to flout Premier League rules, an independent commission has found.

It was confirmed on Tuesday that City had been found guilty of all charges related to “serious breaches” of the league’s financial rules, with the commission also upholding all but one in relation to their failure to co-operate with an investigation spanning over three years.

The commission found that, of £949.94m City claimed in commercial income over a nine-year period, only £119.25m was legitimate, with the remaining £830.69m illicitly paid by their Abu Dhabi owners.

Good evening and welcome to live coverage of the Uefa Nations League match between Czech Republic and England from Slavia Prague’s Eden Stadium. The home side, 49th in the Fifa rankings, scrambled their way to World Cup qualification with victories in the play-offs in penalty shoot-outs over Ireland and Denmark, promptly stank Group A out in Mexico/Canada/United States, drawing with South Africa but losing to South Korea and Mexico to finish last.

Miroslav Koubek, their 74-year-old manager, the oldest in the competition’s history, promptly stood down and has been replaced by their first foreign head coach, Santi, the former Atlético Madrid centre-half, who spent 15 years moving from managing Spain’s U17s, to the U19s and then the U21s. Little wonder, given his CV, that he is looking to refresh his squad with a transfusion of young players, a requirement made all the more urgent by the international retirement of stalwart centre-forward Patrick Schick and the absence of West Ham’s Tomas Soucek who damaged his ankle in that 3-0 defeat by Mexico on June 25 and has not kicked a ball since.

It has been revealed that santi started his stint in charge and this campaign in Group A3 with a 2-1 defeat by Croatia but there were some very positive signs – they set up as a 4-3-3 in classic Spanish/Cruyff style and pressed like dervishes. England, who conceded three goals when players made mistakes when subjected to aggressive pressing in their opening 3-2 defeat by world champions Spain, will have to find better solutions tonight, either by holding their nerve or counterpressing with fewer mistakes.

#153035. Breaking: RANGERS 3 ABERDEEN 2: Amid all the thrills and spills, McInnes' triple switch sparks second-half revival

📅 24 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 7m • 📚 Deep Dive (1364 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Dailymail ↗ Open Full Page

Breaking: RANGERS 3 ABERDEEN 2: Amid all the thrills and spills, McInnes' triple switch sparks second-half revival

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1364 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By JOHN MCGARRY, SCOTTISH CHIEF SPORTS FEATURE WRITER.
  • Published: 18:40 EST, 24 November 2026 | Updated: 18:50 EST, 24 November 2026.
  • When these sides last met in the league at the end of August, Rangers were in such a dark place that you wondered if their season was already destined to be another thoroughly miserable episode.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By JOHN MCGARRY, SCOTTISH CHIEF SPORTS FEATURE WRITER.

Published: 18:40 EST, 24 November 2026 | Updated: 18:50 EST, 24 November 2026.

When these sides last met in the league at the end of August, Rangers were in such a dark place that you wondered if their season was already destined to be another thoroughly miserable episode.

Coming just three days after going out of Europe — for the second time — to an ordinary Jablonec team, the slender win Derek McInnes’ side claimed at Pittodrie that day felt like a can being kicked down the road.

In those early weeks, the players looked lost. The manager admitted that he didn’t know what style of football he was watching. The supporters were preparing for a long, hard winter.

It’s remarkable what can come from one scruffy win on the road. From that point to this, McInnes’ men have now gone 14 games unbeaten in all competitions.

Sources indicate that they have the League Cup final to look forward to next month. They are now just one point behind Celtic in the Premiership and look eminently capable of putting in a serious challenge for the title. In keeping with so many performances throughout this run, however, this wasn’t particularly convincing. Flat and rudderless for 45 minutes, Rangers were deservedly a goal behind at the interval.

Credit where it’s due, though. Their response at the outset of the second period was outstanding with three goals coming in 11 minutes courtesy of Ryan Naderi, Djeidi Gassama and Nico Raskin.

Sources indicate that that ought to have been the platform for many more to follow. But the performance slipped back a level. Aberdeen scored once and could easily have scored again.

Raskin (right) and Gassama celebrate after combining to put Rangers 3-1 up.

Naderi capitalises on Muller's mishandling to fire Rangers level at the start of the second half.

It was a truly thrilling match, full of slip-ups, incidents and moments of brilliance. The final stages were a tough watch for the home fans who hoped against hope that they’d see their side ease towards a routine victory.

Industry observers note that as at Fir Park on Saturday, though, Rangers found a way and added another win to the ledger. And provided that remains the case in the coming weeks and months, none of the light blue legions will be complaining.

Despite ultimately not having quite enough to take something, Aberdeen manager Mario Frick will have been encouraged by much of what he saw here.

Had it not been for that atrocious spell at the outset of the second period, he’d have fancied his men to take something.

They certainly fashioned plenty of opportunities. It was the defensive side of the game which ultimately cost them.

In a recent development, mcInnes drafted in Kevin Kelsy, James Penrice and Ben Godfrey with Dujon Sterling, Tuur Rommens and Kim Minsu dropping out. There was a change of shape too, with a switch to a 3-5-2. For the longest time, it did not work.

Lyons gets his head to Marshall's corner to put Aberdeen in front in the first half.

It has been revealed that while Frick kept faith with the diamond-shaped midfield which served him so well in Ayrshire, he made three changes. In came Ayoub Mouloua, Afeez Aremu and Findlay Marshall at the expense of Hicham Mahou, Ante Palaversa and Stuart Armstrong.

In a recent development, before the game, there was a minute’s silence in memory of the late, great Ralph Brand. What a pity a couple of clowns in the visiting section were unable to keep their mouths shut for that long.

Rangers started brightly with Penrice’s delivery from the left causing chaos. Dan Neil had a stab at it, then Naderi. Aberdeen survived.

Once Frick’s side settled, Nicky Devlin’s cross was met by Marshall. His header was straight at Ivor Pandur.

Rangers’ general play was broken, their build-up more ponderous than patient. Gassama did manage to drop a shoulder and get a strike away but Aremu’s positioning ensured Marius Muller was untroubled.

According to recent reports, naderi was again Rangers’ most effective player, although the bar was set pretty low initially. The Czech’s lay-off invited Godfrey to let fly. His strike was well off target.

It has been revealed that while Gassama got into plenty of promising positions, his crossing continually let him down early on. On the other flank, Badredine Bouanani could not do right for doing wrong.

It has been revealed that when the ball broke kindly to Naderi on the edge of the box, Ibrox expected the net to bulge. This time the man of the moment fired over. Rangers’ efforts in the first half were summed up by Naderi being tripped by Gavin Molloy on the edge of the box. Bouanani’s effort from the free-kick was woeful.

Industry observers note that aberdeen were aggressive and organised. And when the moment arose, they went forward in numbers.

McInnes demonstrates his delight after his half-time changes helped turn the game around.

They edged in front on the half hour after Marshall won a corner which was a consequence of Frick’s men being prepared to back themselves.

According to recent reports, marshall curled the set-piece deep to the far post. Brad Lyons seemed to be invisible to those in light blue as he made a late run. Olwethu Makhanya belatedly reacted but it was too late.

Lyons got enough on his header to beat Pandur and force Raskin to make the block behind his keeper.

The minute the scoreboard indicated that VAR were checking for a goal, you suspected the Belgian hadn’t done quite enough to keep it out. After a lengthy delay came confirmation of that fact.

How would Rangers respond up until the break? Not terribly well. Lyons’ crude foul on Gassama gave Bouanani a chance to make amends with a set-piece. This one smashed into the wall. Seconds later, the winger fired well over the top when he ought to have done better.

The Dons could easily have doubled their advantage. Jack Milne carried well and rattled the ball into Kevin Nisbet’s feet. The forward played a smart pass around the corner. Mouloua was only denied by a terrific save from Pandur.

There was still time for Mouloua to be thwarted by the outstretched leg of Makhanya as he moved to turn home a cut back.

Sources indicate that bluntly, it was no surprise that McInnes made three changes at the break. Off came Godfrey, Kelsy and Bouanani. On went Minsu, Rommens and Findlay Curtis. The impact was extraordinary.

Re-energised, within 45 seconds Rangers were level. Minsu’s speculative shot did come through heavy traffic. Still, Muller had to hold it. Credit to Naderi for anticipating the fumble. The instant it bounced towards him, he instinctively lashed it home for his 10th of the season. Subdued to that point, the home fans roared their approval. And they’d quickly be off their seats again.

As Aberdeen’s attack broke down, Naderi played a simple pass into space. Gassama had too much pace for the chasing pack. Did he have the finishing? Absolutely. What a turnaround.

Gassama squeezes his shot under Muller to put the home side ahead just after the restart.

Industry observers note that two goals in 90 seconds then became three in 11 second-half minutes. Gassama did superbly to motor down the left, look up and play in Raskin. The Belgian smashed the ball back across goal and in.

Industry observers note that that should have been that. Yet three minutes later, the Dons were back within a goal of McInnes’ men. Afforded too much time on the left, Alexander Briedl picked out Marshall with his cross. Marshall swept it home with his left foot via the inside of the post.

In a recent development, remarkably, the Dons might well have levelled. Pandur made a fine save when Minsu threatened to turn an Aberdeen corner into his own net. The ball bounced off Nisbet and just wide.

Terrific throughout, Marshall saw a good strike whistle just wide. The fact the Dons made Rangers sweat for the win will be some consolation.

Upgrade emerges on future of Manchester City’s goalkeepers – it could impact QPR and Pierce Charles

📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (660 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • QPR signed Pierce Charles on loan from Manchester City in the summer, following his switch from Sheffield Wednesday to the Premier League giants.
  • As Charles impresses at Loftus Road, change could await in the goalkeeping department back at his parent club.
  • It has been revealed that rulli, 34, is only cover, but Donnarumma has drawn criticism for his shortcomings in possession, given that City need a goalkeeper who is comfortable in helping in build-up phases.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

QPR signed Pierce Charles on loan from Manchester City in the summer, following his switch from Sheffield Wednesday to the Premier League giants. The 20-year-old was viewed as a big talent before this season, but his starring performances for the Hoops have put the wider footballing world on notice.

As Charles impresses at Loftus Road, change could await in the goalkeeping department back at his parent club. The Athletic tips Manchester City to make changes in between the sticks by moving out both Gianluigi Donnarumma and backup Geronimo Rulli in 2027.

It has been revealed that rulli, 34, is only cover, but Donnarumma has drawn criticism for his shortcomings in possession, given that City need a goalkeeper who is comfortable in helping in build-up phases. This is undoubtedly Charles’ standout attribute, and it may well see him accelerated into first-team contention at the Etihad Stadium.

To make it clear, there is nothing suggested about a Charles recall from QPR in The Athletic’s latest report. In October, it was confirmed that Manchester City have an option to bring him back in January if they wish, but there were no plans at the time.

It has been revealed that regular EFL viewers have known about Charles’ potential for some time. He emerged on the first-team stage at Sheffield Wednesday and promptly impressed with his distribution, showing composure beyond his years and a passing range that wouldn’t look out of place in midfield.

According to recent reports, those same attributes in possession have been on show with the Hoops, but Charles is growing in confidence in commanding his box and claiming crosses too. A save percentage of 67.8% demonstrates there is still room for improvement with regard to shot-stopping (FotMob).

Recent findings suggest that however, Charles’ passing abilities make him an ideal fit for Manchester City’s style, and he seems bound to get a chance in the future. Accuracy is one thing, but the Northern Irishman’s technique sees means he can play flat balls into the attackers too, allowing them to bring it down on their chest or with their feet rather than challenging for headers with big Championship centre-backs.

This allows QPR to get the ball forward quickly and keep it there. It is a rare ability in goalkeepers, and one that will not go unnoticed at Manchester City.

Manchester City need a goalkeeper comfortable in build-up, and Charles is just that. However, at this moment in time, it would be a big risk to pull him from his QPR loan and throw him into the starting lineup.

As touched on before, his save percentage shows he still needs to improve as a shot-stopper. The progress he is making in West London suggests he can grow and become a starting option for City further down the line, but at present, the areas he still has to improve could be exposed at an elite level.

It means the Hoops should be confident of keeping Charles for the season – it would be best for him to stay for the full campaign too.

Industry observers note that however, in the interest of staying prepared, it might be wise for the R’s to eye potential replacements. That way, if Manchester City do make a bold move to recall Charles, they are ready to act swiftly when January comes around.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, derby County are rooted to the bottom of the Championship table coming into this weekend’s games, and there is huge pressure on head coach John Eustace.
  • In a recent development, it feels like a must-win match for Eustace, who has been under growing pressure from supporters.
  • One man who has been near ever-present in the Rams’ struggling backline is Dion Sanderson.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, derby County are rooted to the bottom of the Championship table coming into this weekend’s games, and there is huge pressure on head coach John Eustace. However, he remains in post and will lead DCFC for their home game against fellow strugglers Watford on Saturday.

In a recent development, it feels like a must-win match for Eustace, who has been under growing pressure from supporters. The season has been a tough one all-round at Pride Park, but with 35 goals conceded in 17 games, they have the joint-worst defence in the league.

One man who has been near ever-present in the Rams’ struggling backline is Dion Sanderson. Against Watford, Eustace has to consider pulling the 26-year-old from the starting lineup.

Sanderson has made 15 Championship appearances this season, starting all of them. He has played the full 90 minutes on all but two occasions, being taken off at half-time against West Brom and seeing red after 66 minutes in the 1-1 draw against Sheffield United.

In a recent development, sanderson was a hit with Derby County last season and he has proven his ability in the Championship across 169 appearances at the level, so Eustace has good reason to believe the defender can deliver. However, the facts are that he hasn’t this season.

Recent findings suggest that the former Birmingham City man has won only 51.3% of his duels, ranking him in the bottom 17% of Championship defenders. DCFC have conceded 28.13 xG with Sanderson on the pitch (bottom 2%) as well, although this is more of an indication of how bad the backline has been as a unit (FotMob).

Eustace has been limited in his ability to make defensive changes, but that is not the case anymore.

It has been revealed that matt Clarke returned to the team against Wolves, and Eiran Cashin was back on the bench. Those two, alongside free transfer signings Shane Duffy and Jack Robinson, mean that Derby County have the depth to make alterations in a bid to find form.

Recent findings suggest that duffy has impressed since joining, so it could be him and Clarke started in a centre-back pairing. If Eustace goes for a three at the back, it should be the fit-again Cashin or Robinson to join them in the side, not Sanderson.

In a recent development, derby County desperately need some hope. The 3-1 win over Bolton Wanderers gave them a boost, but consecutive defeats to Southampton and Wolves have dampened spirits again.

It has been revealed that as rival clubs make changes in the dugout, DCFC have stuck by Eustace. However, that could change with a home defeat to Watford.

This is a winnable game, and you get the feeling that three points are a must. If not, Eustace could be sacked.

That could prompt changes from the boss, who will do all he can to drive a performance from his struggling side as pressure and relegation fears grow.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Hibernian ended their long wait for a Premiership home win after overcoming Dundee in a hard-fought contest at Easter Road.
  • Martin Boyle and Nicky Cadden – who curled home a stunning effort from outside the box – had the hosts in command before the interval.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Published: 18:46 EST, 24 November 2026 | Updated: 18:51 EST, 24 November 2026.

Hibernian ended their long wait for a Premiership home win after overcoming Dundee in a hard-fought contest at Easter Road.

Martin Boyle and Nicky Cadden – who curled home a stunning effort from outside the box – had the hosts in command before the interval.

But Dundee, still licking their wounds after an 8-0 savaging at the hands of Hearts on Saturday, demonstrated plenty of fight after the break and pulled one back through Joe Wright.

The visitors tried in vain to grab an equaliser and it was Hibs who were left satisfied by their first three points at home since beating Kilmarnock on April 4.

Manager Marink Reedijk was thrilled to have bounced back from their 4-0 weekend home defeat at the hands of Dundee United, saying: ‘I think it’s a good reaction to what we have done against Dundee United.

Sources indicate that ‘It’s crucial that you get the three points at home. Again, that’s a big win. I saw a front foot team again, I saw togetherness again, I saw a team who fought for every ball.

Martin Boyle takes the acclaim after scoring the all-important second goal for Hibernian.

‘That’s not easy, they have to be patient, you have to be secure, you have to wait for your moment and we took these moments and that was really good to see.

Industry observers note that ‘The goal of Nicky [Cadden] is one to, we say, put in a frame and put on your wall as a painting. The one of Martin [Boyle] is why Martin is so important for us. He can disrupt an opponent if they are so organised and so close to each other and so deep.

‘As long as we keep ourselves, I think these are good signs.’.

Hibs played on the front foot as they looked to start repairing the damage from the weekend. On a rare start, Togo international Thibault Klidje was lively and saw a header crash into the side-netting before hitting a harmless snap-shot straight at Dundee goalkeeper Owen Goodman.

From a short corner routine Hibs worked space for Cadden on the edge of the box from Josh Mulligan’s lay-off and his driving effort whistled just past a post.

It has been revealed that dundee were desperate to keep it tight at the back but offered little going forward. Just when it looked like they were beginning to settle Hibs hit them with two goals in three minutes before the break.

The first came in the 40th minute when Boyle fired a penalty past Goodman after being tripped by Ryan Finnigan.

Nicky Cadden unleashes an absolute pearler into the top corner to put Hibs in front.

Industry observers note that cadden then found the top corner with a sublime curling effort from his left foot just outside the box. It was another short corner routine that saw Miguel Chaiwa set up the wing-back.

Despite the hammer blow of losing two goals in quick succession before the break, Dundee demonstrated at the start of the second half that they were not going to roll over.

Steven Pressley’s side upped their intensity as they searched for a goal to get themselves back in the game and that arrived in the 67th minute courtesy of Wright.

Substitute Callum Jones’ free-kick should have been put away by Ryan Astley but the ball broke back to Wright and he slammed the ball high into the net from six yards.

That set up a tense finish but Hibs desperately held on for a rare home victory.

For Pressley, who changed half of his outfield XI following his side’s weekend humiliation, there were also positives to take.

Sources indicate that the Dark Blues boss noted: ‘We’re disappointed to not come away with anything and to obviously lose the game. But I also thought we restored some degree of pride tonight.

‘Going into half-time 2-0 down, losing two late goals in the half, can be a little bit demoralising, especially for a team that has a bit of fragility on the back of the weekend’s result.

Recent findings suggest that ‘I thought we responded brilliantly. We showed a lot of courage, a lot of determination, a lot of spirit and, as I’ve said, I think we certainly restored some level of pride that allows us a foundation to move into the weekend.’.

Breaking: Russell must do something wacky now after disappointing Bahrain GP qualifying

📅 03 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 25 min read (5018 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~25 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Never mind the lack of an ice vest, George Russell is somehow going to need to be the coolest man in Malaysia if he is to turn seventh on the grid into a positive result in Sunday’s Bahrain Grand Prix.The first race in Sepang in nearly a decade – a late addition to the calendar because of the conflict in the Middle East – promises to be an absolute scorcher.
  • It will be the first time since Hungary 2023 that those two gladiators have started on a front row together.
  • Russell might need something wacky if he is to do anything from that far back.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Never mind the lack of an ice vest, George Russell is somehow going to need to be the coolest man in Malaysia if he is to turn seventh on the grid into a positive result in Sunday’s Bahrain Grand Prix.The first race in Sepang in nearly a decade – a late addition to the calendar because of the conflict in the Middle East – promises to be an absolute scorcher. It might even be worth setting your alarm for the 8am UK start time. Red Bull’s Max Verstappen will start in pole position for the first time this year. He will have Ferrari’s Lewis Hamilton alongside him.

It will be the first time since Hungary 2023 that those two gladiators have started on a front row together. Throw in sweltering temperatures, low grip, high tyre degradation, and the ever-present threat of a Malaysian monsoon sweeping through Sepang, and you have the potential for fireworks.

Russell might need something wacky if he is to do anything from that far back. This was a desperately disappointing result for the British driver. After his victory in Baku last weekend, Russell was hopeful he had finally found the winning formula and that he could continue to take the fight to his team-mate Kimi Antonelli, whom he trails in the drivers’ championship by 66pts.

It has been revealed that eighth, four places behind, and 0.24sec slower than the Italian, was not what Russell would have had in mind, although both Mercedes drivers will rise a spot because of the five-place grid penalty meted out to Red Bull’s Isack Hadjar for exceeding his engine allowance for the season.Russell will have felt particularly disappointed as Antonelli only got one run in Q3 after using up a set of soft tyres when he made a mistake and went off track in Q2. He now trails his team mate nine-seven in qualifying head-to-head this year.“No to be honest,” Russell admitted when asked whether he knew why he was so slow. “This circuit is an outlier in terms of the abrasiveness of the tarmac.“The lap times seven years ago were six or seven seconds faster and at certain points on the track it feels like you are driving on gravel, which is the same for everyone, but it is clearly affecting us more than others.”Mercedes’ lack of performance was doubly unexpected because not only did they arrive here with a massive upgrade package, but Russell revealed this week that he and Antonelli were foregoing the cooling vests you see some drivers sporting on the grid, in favour of car performance.

Toto Wolff, the Mercedes team principal, admitted it was a head-scratcher. “Very difficult to understand,” the Austrian remarked. “We have been a little bit caught out on Friday with some car behaviour that we did not see all year, but then you can say it is very hot and the tarmac is different to all the [other] tracks. It looked really good this morning. We seemed to have, at least with Kimi, made a step in understanding. And then, qualifying was a little bit back to what we saw before, just no performance.”.

It has been revealed that still, both titles are in the bag so Wolff cannot be too unhappy. Russell is the one who will be really miffed. He really needs to be beating his team-mate pretty much every race weekend if he is to get his title hopes back on track.

At the front, the mood was somewhat different. Verstappen became the first non-Mercedes-powered pilot to take a pole position this year. It was a first pole position for Red Bull Powertrains, too. And with his long run pace looking more than decent, Verstappen should really hold on for his first win of 2026. Hamilton will do his best to hang on to the Dutchman’s coattails. The seven-time champion was delighted when told he had taken P2. “Let’s go guys! Finally! Great job guys, really great job. Car felt great.”.

In a recent development, this was indeed an excellent performance from the Ferrari man – and just the tonic for the Scuderia after weeks of gossip and speculation. Hamilton was admittedly three tenths slower than his rival, which he put purely down to a power deficit on the straights, but he noted he was hopeful his long run pace was more competitive. The last time a F1 held a race was held here back in 2017, the British driver claimed pole only to be overhauled by a youthful Verstappen. He will be desperate to turn the tables this time.

Recent findings suggest that “It was really hard to find a good balance, and we made one change before qualifying and we hit the sweet spot,” he reflected afterwards. “I am so, so grateful. I will try my best to hold on to Max tomorrow, and if we are in the fight that would be awesome. I’ve been talking too much, but I guess you talk more when you are happy. It was my best lap of the year. It feels like I won, and I will give it everything tomorrow.”.

It is Russell, though, who needs a result even more badly if he is to remain a factor in the championship. “As a team, we have yet to have a bad race this whole season and this was clearly a very bad qualifying for us,” he admitted, adding that “all the numbers” from the upgrade package suggested it was an improvement on the old car. “But I think there is going to be a lot happening tomorrow. The tyre deg is huge and race pace will be king. So even though today was a real disappointment it is not the be all and end all.”.

No. 1 ☝️#F1 #BahrainGP pic.twitter.com/01PqrckQS9.

According to recent reports, tomorrow’s race will be the first time since Hungary 2023 that Max Verstappen and Lewis Hamilton will start on the front row together. It is a reasonable run down to turn one and there are overtaking opportunities through the first few corners at Sepang, with it being similar to the configuration in China, with plenty of lines and moves on offer.

Respect between two great champions 🤩#F1 #BahrainGP pic.twitter.com/fbZ6aoKRyw.

It has been revealed that “Very difficult to understand. We have been a little bit caught out on Friday with some car behaviour that we did not see all year, but then you can say it is very hot and the tarmac is the different to all the (other) tracks. It looked really good this morning. We seemed to have, at least with Kimi [Antonelli], made a step in understanding. And then, qualifying was a little bit back to what we saw before, just no performance.”.

On Kimi Antonelli’s track limits breach in Q2:.

“Not good, because Q2 you know you are going to get through. You lose a set [of softs] in a qualifying that is so tight, where we are on the back foot. That is not good.”.

In a recent development, lewis Hamilton states this is the biggest crowd he has ever seen at Sepang, thanking the fans for making it here today. That is actually a bigger compliment than many watching at home may realise. The traffic this weekend has been horrendous. After 10 years without a race in Malaysia, during which time F1 has grown massively, I think they have forgotten how to do traffic management. Shuttles are inconsistent, taxis can’t get in/out, it’s taking forever just to reach the airport a few kilometres away - some fans have been braving the heat and walking. It took over two hours to get back into Kuala Lumpur last night (48km). My understanding is the Bahrainis are organising the race this year, while local forces are handling the traffic outside the circuit.

“The car has been very good since last week. It is good to come back [from his wrist injury] at such a time and I am enjoying it, fighting for the top three. Even though it was not my finest qualifying session it is a good feeling.

“It is a bit unfortunate we take a penalty on a track where we are that fast but, from eighth, I am confident we can come through the field and come back for a good result.”.

Recent findings suggest that “I love this energy [from the crowd]. Major, big thank you to Malaysia for welcoming us. It is so hot here. I keep saying it, but that has made it a massive challenge for the tyres, the car, the mechanics in the garage. I am really, really thankful to my team. We made so many changes through all these practice sessions. Because the cars are sliding, the tyres are overheating, it was really hard to find a good balance, and we made one last change going into qualifying and I think we hit the sweet spot. To be able to close the gap to two or three tenths to Max [Verstappen], who has been so quick all weekend, is great, and I am so grateful.

“I am much happier with where the car is, but tomorrow is a completely different ballgame. Making these tyres last around this track, they are overheating from the get-go. Every little bit of wheelspin you have, every little snap you have makes a difference of how far you are going to go. I like to think we have got a good balance. Max was really quick on his long runs, so I will just try my best to hold onto him tomorrow.”.

A reminder that Isack Hadjar will drop from third to eighth after his grid penalty.

QUALIFYING CLASSIFICATIONCan't wait for Sunday! 🤩#F1 #BahrainGP pic.twitter.com/qqi8hPDcKA.

“It is fantastic. We have been trying many grand prix to get pole. Sometimes a bit closer than others but to finally get it, from where we started the season, pretty incredible. I am happy with today and, for sure, I am going to try and win tomorrow. When you start first, that is the target.”.

Significant disappointment that for Russell. After his win in Baku, where he noted he finally felt hooked up to the car, he was desperate to build the momentum. P8, four places behind Antonelli, was not what he would have had in mind. Has it all to do in the race tomorrow.

Excellent (though not unexpected) pole for Verstappen, and a very good P2 for Hamilton. Could be some fireworks on the front row tomorrow.

*Hadjar’s three-place grid penalty will drop him down to eighth place for the race tomorrow.

In a recent development, neither of the Red Bulls can improve in the first sector but it is those behind them who need significant improvements. The two Ferraris are going along nicely at the start of their final flying laps. Hadjar is unable to improve despite a purple final sector. Verstappen then goes fastest in the final sector and improves his advantage at the top.

Recent findings suggest that hamilton meanwhile went fastest in the middle sector and goes second fastest overall. Piastri cannot improve but stays ahead of Russell.

Norris is the final man across the line but is only fast enough for P6. That means that Verstappen takes pole in Malaysia, which is the first time this season that Red Bull have taken pole position. Hamilton is second with Hadjar third, although the Frenchman has a five-place grid penalty.

Sources indicate that MAX VERSTAPPEN TAKES POLE FOR THE BAHRAIN GRAND PRIX IN MALAYSIA!! 👊#F1 #BahrainGP pic.twitter.com/NgtaCAZacL.

The two Red Bulls, who are one and two at the moment, will be the first two drivers across the line on these final efforts.

It has been revealed that the other nine drivers in Q3 are in the pits so young Antonelli has the track to himself as he sets his one and only flying lap of Q3. He is over four tenths down on Verstappen through the first sector and has plenty of work to do.

The championship leader sets a decent middle sector where he loses no more time to Verstappen. As it stands he would put himself third before the others do their final runs. He comes across the line in P3 but will have the likes of Hamilton, Piastri, Leclerc, Norris and Russell trying to surpass him.

Russell is the first across the line and sets a time of a 1:36.032. He does not last long at the top as he is immediately displaced by Hadjar, who is half a second quicker.

According to recent reports, hamilton then comes over the line in second, just ahead of his teammate Leclerc. Piastri puts himself between the two Ferraris.

What about Verstappen? The man who won here the last time we were in Malaysia continues his great form today and goes quickest by more than three tenths.

Industry observers note that antonelli now heads out and will have the track to himself really. This is going to be the championship leader’s only flying lap of Q3.

Industry observers note that russell is the first man to head out for his first flying lap in Q3. Antonelli has remained in the pits with just one fresh set of softs remaining. Verstappen, who right now feels like the favourite for pole, will be one of the last across the line in these first attempts of Q3.

The fight for pole position in Sepang begins now as the green light is on at the end of the pit lane to get Q3 going.

Antonelli, due to that lap time deletion in Q2, has just one new set of softs for Q3, which could prove costly in his attempts to try and take pole.

Recent findings suggest that P12 the best qualifying result of the season for Alonso. It was only his second time in Q2 after Hungary (P16).

In a recent development, I should add, P14 was also Lance Stroll’s best qualifying result of the season. His first outing in Q2 this year.

Sources indicate that 11. Liam Lawson (Racing Bulls)12. Fernando Alonso (Aston Martin)13. Carlos Sainz (Williams)14. Lance Stroll (Aston Martin)15. Franco Colapinto (Alpine)16. Arvid Lindblad (Racing Bulls).

With grid penalties already on their way, neither Colapinto nor Lindblad set lap times in Q2.

Verstappen, Leclerc, Piastri, Norris, Hadjar and Russell all remain in the pits. A bit of a risk for Russell down in eighth but his time should be enough to get into Q3.

Lindblad, who will start tomorrow’s race at the back of the grid after penalties, gives his teammate Lawson a tow down the back straight and it works as Lawson just sneaks into the top ten.

Can Bortoleto get back ahead though of Lawson? Yes he can and he will take the final place in Q3. Lawson thought he might be through but the tow was not enough.

Lindblad, who's taking a grid penalty for Sunday's race, gave team mate Lawson a tow but it wasn't quite enough to send the Kiwi into Q3#F1 #BahrainGP pic.twitter.com/IMlrqg4ENv.

As the young Italian starts his flying lap, there is no-one else out on track so no traffic. He is a lot more cautious at turn six this time than last time, when he had his lap time deleted.

He has not set blistering first and second sector times but a purple final sector puts him into second and the Italian is safely into Q3.

Plenty of other drivers are now heading around the track for their final flying laps of Q2.

11. Lance Stroll (Aston Martin)12. Carlos Sainz (Williams)13. Kimi Antonelli (Mercedes)14. Arvid Lindblad (Racing Bulls)15. Franco Colapinto (Alpine)16. Fernando Alonso (Aston Martin).

Mercedes have put a brand new set of softs onto Antonelli’s car as he heads out promptly, with no lap time to his name so far. Antonelli is still disputing the lap deletion over team radio but his team tell him the images show he exceeded track limits. This is now a lot of pressure on the championship leader; any mistake now and he will not make Q3. His teammate Russell is only in seventh.

Sources indicate that antonelli was fourth fastest but has had his lap time deleted for exceeding track limits at turn six. That is a substantial moment in Q2 and could prove problematic if he gets into Q3. Antonelli appeared to be confused when he was told about his lap deletion over team radio but the on-board view looked pretty clear-cut.

Piastri then comes across the line in third.

Here's the moment Kimi ran wide 👀#F1 #BahrainGP pic.twitter.com/E0VdWdBt8x.

Recent findings suggest that the Dutchman looks in a great spot at the moment to take pole position today and his 1:35.696 is very quick. He is nearly four tenths quicker than Antonelli.

How about the Ferraris? Leclerc was quickest in the middle sector but is nearly three tenths down on Verstappen. Hamilton puts himself into third place. Russell is more than half a second down on Verstappen.

Verstappen has been shown a black and white flag for driving unnecessarily slowly. I doubt he will get a grid penalty for that but it will be a warning for the Dutchman.

Anyway, the drivers, other than Colapinto and Alonso, are on flying laps, with Verstappen at the moment fastest inthe first sector.

Industry observers note that the green light is showing at the end of the pit lane and the second part of qualifying is under way. Like the start of Q1, it is hardly a stampede to go out.

Sources indicate that 17. Nico Hulkenberg (Audi)18. Oliver Bearman (Haas)19. Esteban Ocon (Haas)20. Alex Albon (Williams)21. Valtteri Bottas (Cadillac)22. Sergio Perez (Cadillac).

The Aston Martin of Stroll improves significantly from 20th and is set to make Q2, as is his teammate Alonso. A bit of a surprise to see the Aston Martins improve and make it into Q2.

Go Fernando! 🤩 Go Lance! 🤩First double Q2 appearance this season 🙌#F1 #BahrainGP pic.twitter.com/xjiWYv6ycr.

Industry observers note that that has seen the Audi of Hulkenberg drop into the drop zone and the German is out. For contrast, his teammate improves to go into eighth place! Hulkenberg had a substantial lock up into turn 14, which proved very costly.

As it stands, eight of the top nine are remaining in the garage. Russell is in ninth and has not gone out but Gasly above him in eighth has. You would imagine Russell is perfectly safe.

17. Esteban Ocon (Haas)18. Alex Albon (Williams)19. Oliver Bearman (Haas)20. Lance Stroll (Aston Martin)21. Valtteri Bottas (Cadillac)22. Sergio Perez (Cadillac).

Ocon, in 17th, is quite far off Hulkenberg in 16th and needs more than four tenths to usurp him.

The screens in the media centre here in Sepang tell me that the air temp right now is 32.8C and the track temp is 58C. It feels even hotter. Lots of chat about cooling vests this week, which are optional. George Russell is among the drivers who isn’t using one, which is interesting a) because Russell has suffered badly from heat in the past (Qatar, Singapore) and b) because he says Mercedes chose to put the development money into car upgrades instead.

It’s an interesting admission. Not everyone is sold on the idea of cooling vests. Ferrari and McLaren will definitely be using them this weekend, for instance. Max Verstappen won’t as he doesn’t like them. Russell thinks the FIA should just develop the tech themselves and it shouldn’t be part of the budget cap.

In a recent development, “Our team have put a lot of emphasis this year on the cockpit temperature,” he said. “We won’t be running the cooling vest because we haven’t put the resource into making it robust enough. I feel we need the FIA just to step in and say ‘Here’s some money extra in the cost cap or there’s an external tech giant who’s going to develop it for everybody’. Because we should all be wearing it. When it works, it works great. So, I would like to wear it this week, and I would like to wear it next week. But the team asked me...look, we can develop it, and we can put the money towards it...[but at a cost].

Industry observers note that he added: “The top itself is not expensive ..you’ve got to effectively make a system where you can fit a block of dry ice or actual ice, and then has the airflow to circulate the cool water throughout. If that system isn’t robust enough, then suddenly you have no circulation, and then you get hot. You get ambient temperature circulating. The vest is one-design, but the system that circulates the water is different [at different teams].”.

Recent findings suggest that the two Ferraris are on medium tyres but Leclerc still puts himself into second place. He is then displaced by Hamilton, who slots in behind Verstappen. Good times from the Ferraris on the mediums.

Industry observers note that what about the McLarens? Norris goes sixth fastest but is more than six tenths down on Verstappen. Then comes Piastri, who goes fourth fastest, just under four tenths off Verstappen.

Arguably the three favourites for pole; Antonelli, Russell and Verstappen, are all on flying laps.

The first sector goes the way of Verstappen, who is purple, and then the Dutchman goes purple in the middle sector.

Antonelli is two tenths faster than his teammate Russell but Verstappen is over half a second quicker than the Mercedes. Hadjar is then second fastest to show the pace in the Red Bull this weekend.

Most of the teams waited and waited to come out and then suddenly lots of drivers are sent out, resulting in a queue in the pits! With the high track temperatures and high degradation, the drivers are crawling around on their out laps to preserve these soft tyres.

Recent findings suggest that bumper to bumper in the pit lane! #F1 #BahrainGP pic.twitter.com/ff8JO9kB1g.

According to recent reports, the two Haas drivers have a free track to themselves whilst everyone else bides their time. In theory, as the hour of qualifying goes on, the track temperature should decrease and the more rubber that is laid down the faster the track should get.

Finally, just before the two Haas drivers finish their first flying laps, the rest of the grid is starting to emerge, led by the Mercedes duo.

Industry observers note that the green light is showing at the end of the pit lane and Q1 is officially under way. The two Haas drivers are the first to head out. Other than that, it is a quiet start to Q1.

Industry observers note that the top four teams; Mercedes, Red Bull, Ferrari and McLaren, all have a genuine chance of taking pole in Sepang today. I think the true favourites though have to be the Mercedes duo and Max Verstappen but with how close it between all four of the teams you cannot rule anything out.

It is 33 degrees celsius air temperature, with the track temperature up at 58 degrees.

Not long to wait now until qualifying begins. It is hot, humid and dry in Sepang right now. As we know in Malaysia, the weather can change promptly and thunderstorms can roll in quite quickly but it looks like today’s qualifying will be a dry one. This will be one of if not the hottest qualifying sessions of the season, so much so that we are seeing umbrellas going up to get some shade from the sun rather than sheltering from any rain.

This will be important to consider after qualifying finishes as there will be some shuffling around:.

Isack Hadjar (Red Bull): five-place grid penalty- newly introduced internal combustion engineFranco Colapinto (Alpine): ten-place grid penalty- new engineFranco Colapinto (Alpine): five-place grid penalty- causing a collision in BakuArvid Lindblad (Racing Bulls): back of the grid- complete power unit change.

Hadjar has looked good since returning from his wrist injury so could be fighting it out near the front of the grid, although his five-place penalty will drop him down. We know Lindblad will be at the back and is very likely to be joined there by Colapinto, who is not going to be qualifying high up in the top ten in his Alpine.

According to recent reports, haas have announced that Frenchman Esteban Ocon will leave at the end of this season. Ocon now faces an uncertain future, with it difficult to see a spot for him on the F1 grid next season. There are suggestions that the 30-year-old’s replacement will be Brazilian Ferrari junior Rafael Camara, although nothing has been confirmed on that front. 21-year-old Camara currently leads the Formula 2 championship.

TGR Haas F1 Team and Esteban Ocon will part ways at the conclusion of the 2026 season. With plenty of racing ahead, our focus remains on working together to maximize every opportunity through to the final race of the year.#HaasF1 #F1 pic.twitter.com/4iQAuqnSyA.

Aston Martin have now confirmed their driver line-up for next season, retaining both Fernando Alonso and Lance Stroll. There had been reports that Alonso had been contemplating retirement but the 45-year-old will continue into another season.

Aston Martin Aramco confirms Lance and Fernando will continue as the team's drivers in 2027. Read more: ​https://t.co/ePyjJdyAIB pic.twitter.com/VogFUEbNxy.

Other than the second seat alongside Ollie Bearman at Haas, the only other team to keep an eye on is Racing Bulls, with no definite confirmation on their exact driver line-up for next season.

Recent findings suggest that ferrari this week have publicly backed their team principal Frederic Vasseur, amid speculation over the Frenchman’s position and comments made by former Red Bull team principal Christian Horner, who said the job at Ferrari would be a “dream job”. Ferrari, who sit second in the constructors’ standings, have not won the drivers’ championship since 2007 (Kimi Raikkonen) and the constructors’ since 2008. Here is a snippet from Tom Cary’s piece on the matter:.

In a hastily convened media call on Tuesday morning, Maria Conti, Ferrari’s chief communication officer, noted the Scuderia had decided to issue a vote of confidence in Vasseur in response “not just to the story of Mr Horner, but in general, the speculation about Fred”.

“Ferrari has made its choices,” Conti said. “We have confidence – full confidence – in Fred Vasseur and in his team, and we continue to do so.

“At this time, it’s really crucial that the team remains united and cohesive, and we are focused with all the energy on the work ahead.”.

“It is great to be back [in Malaysia]. I am really enjoying the track. We have had some wonderful races here over time. It is actually the 20th time we have been here, it started in 1999, and it is really exciting to be back. I really enjoyed getting out on the track and watching the cars closely.

Industry observers note that “The drivers are super fit and they have some cooling but it is not easy. But you almost cannot get enough fluid through your body before your stomach gives up. Having this race and Singapore back-to-back increases that challenge.”.

Especially with the significant upgrade they have brought this weekend, Mercedes’ lead at the summit is looking unassailable right now.

Sources indicate that almost nine years ago to the day, Max Verstappen took just his second race victory in Formula 1. Lewis Hamilton, who took pole position, and Daniel Ricciardo joined Verstappen on the podium. Despite being nine years ago, plenty of drivers still on the grid were racing that weekend. Here they are and who they were racing for:.

Max Verstappen (Red Bull) Lewis Hamilton (Mercedes) Valtteri Bottas (Mercedes) Esteban Ocon (Force India)Nico Hulkenberg (Renault)Sergio Perez (Force India)Fernando Alonso (McLaren)Lance Stroll (Williams)Carlos Sainz (Toro Rosso)Pierre Gasly (Toro Rosso).

Recent findings suggest that with Russell winning in Baku and Antonelli finishing fifth, the latter’s championship lead was cut to 66 points. If Russell is going to usurp his teammate, he is going to need a few more similar results to last weekend due to the size of Antonelli’s lead. If Antonelli were to suffer a retirement, then that completely changes the outlook.

In a recent development, formula One returns to Malaysia for round 16 of the season for the Bahrain Grand Prix. That probably sounds strange but after the Bahrain Grand Prix was originally postponed in March, F1 reinstated it to the calendar with Malaysia hosting it because of the ongoing war in the Middle East. Despite being held in Malaysia, Bahrain have retained the naming rights for the event, which is officially known as the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia. The last time Formula One was in Malaysia was nine years ago back in 2017, when a young whippersnapper named Max Verstappen, still four years away from winning his first world championship, claimed just his second victory.

Sources indicate that last time out around the streets of Baku, Mercedes’ George Russell claimed victory at the Azerbaijan Grand Prix, pipping Verstappen by just a tenth of a second. That was Russell’s first grand prix win since June and cuts his team-mate Kimi Antonelli’s lead in the drivers’ standings to 66 points. Antonelli had a challenging weekend in Baku, starting 16th after a crash in qualifying and coming home in fifth to see his championship lead to Russell cut by 15 points.

According to recent reports, verstappen was quickest in first practice yesterday, with the Ferrari of Charles Leclerc fastest in second practice. Earlier today, championship leader Antonelli was nearly three tenths clear of the field in third practice. Mercedes, 160 points clear at the top of the constructors’ standings, have brought significant upgrades this weekend, which includes a latest floor, rear suspension and rear corner. It is the team’s first significant car upgrade since the Canadian Grand at the end of May.

This race in Malaysia represents the second leg of the season’s first flyaway triple header, with the Singapore Grand Prix to come next weekend, so the demands on the teams and the drivers are incredibly high. Qualifying from Sepang gets under way at 9am (GMT).

26-year-old steps up to prove his value in absence of influential Blackburn Rovers man: Opinion

📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (598 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Blackburn Rovers have maintained solid form since the international break, drawing with Burnley before a midweek win over Watford.
  • Injury to Sam Morsy also presented a dilemma for Rovers.
  • However, on hand to step up and soften the blow of Morsy’s absence has been Moussa Baradji.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Blackburn Rovers have maintained solid form since the international break, drawing with Burnley before a midweek win over Watford. They’ve had to deal with adversity ahead of those matches too, notably seeing head coach Tony Mowbray step back from his duties for health reasons.

Injury to Sam Morsy also presented a dilemma for Rovers. Since moving to Ewood Park in the summer, the 35-year-old has emerged as a leader and formed a fine partnership with Kristi Montgomery in the middle of the park.

However, on hand to step up and soften the blow of Morsy’s absence has been Moussa Baradji. After some challenging moments in his debut campaign, the 26-year-old midfielder has delivered when needed and proven his value in the Rovers squad.

Baradji joined Blackburn Rovers on an initial loan last summer, and he had to deal with injury in his first season. His impact was limited as a result, and when he was available, fans weren’t too sold on his performances.

Despite this, the Frenchman was signed permanently in the summer. When injury hit and Baradji missed the first six games of the latest Championship season, many of the Rovers faithful feared a similar campaign would pan out.

However, Baradji has now played in all of the last 10 Championship games – four have come from the start, two when covering for Montgomery during his injury absence, and two while Morsy has been out. The last two appearances have been the best of the lot, battling hard to help Rovers to a point against Burnley before another well-rounded display in the mature midweek win over Watford.

Baradji has brought power in and out of possession in Morsy’s absence. He isn’t afraid to get stuck in and use his stature to muscle opponents off the ball, and his physical attributes, paired with slick footwork, make him a good ball carrier as well.

Recent findings suggest that the midfielder’s per 90 stats highlight the impression he has made when called upon. As per FotMob‘s dataset, Baradji is averaging 1.30 successful dribbles per 90 (top 9% of Championship midfielders), 9.88 duels won (top 1%), 7.64 defensive contributions (top 8%) and a 75% long-ball accuracy rate (top 4%).

Sources indicate that baradji’s signing came with some reservations, as a deal was initially shelved when his medical raised an injury problem. However, the numbers he posted in a competitive Swiss Super League for a relegated Yverdon Sport side showed exactly why Blackburn Rovers were interested.

And, his recent performances have started to show that he can be a hit in the Championship too. Baradji pairs power and skill to offer a real force in possession, and his work rate and physicality have seen him offer the strong presence needed in the middle in Morsy’s absence.

Morsy will be backed to reclaim his place when fit. But, at 35, he isn’t a long-term option. Baradji has shown he is ready to stake a claim for a long-term spot in the Rovers team.

Arsenal's winning run at the Emirates is over.

They had been on a mental run of wins at home in both the Champions League and Europa League. Like, I mean truly crazy. But now it's come to an end.

Industry observers note that they have failed to win a home game in the group stage of major European competition for the first time since November 2019 (2-1 defeat vs Eintracht Frankfurt). Yep, seven years... told you it was mental.

Tonight's draw ends a run of 18 successive victories – the longest such winning run by any side in major European competition history.

I bet Borussia Dortmund just can't wait to get out of London.

Tonight is yet another evening where they have struggled playing in England - they never seem to do well here.

Leicester City could lose loan star in January as parent club consider recall

📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (533 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Leicester City sit 7th in League One ahead of this weekend’s clash with Mansfield Town.
  • Form has picked up in recent weeks but as the January window gets closer, talk of departures has ramped up.
  • According to recent reports, howell has featured primarily from the bench in League One this season, making just the one start.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Leicester City sit 7th in League One ahead of this weekend’s clash with Mansfield Town. Russell Martin’s side have picked up 23 points from 15 matches, winning six, drawing five and losing four.

Form has picked up in recent weeks but as the January window gets closer, talk of departures has ramped up. One of which could be loanee Harry Howell, who Brighton are considering recalling from LCFC, according to Pete O’Rourke.

According to recent reports, howell has featured primarily from the bench in League One this season, making just the one start. In all competitions he has two goal contributions in 13 games for the Foxes.

Recent findings suggest that brighton are considering a recall to send Howell elsewhere in January in a bid to get more game-time. A host of clubs both in England and across Europe are keen on the 18-year-old.

Howell’s loan spell at LCFC has so far failed to provide the regular senior football Brighton wanted for his development. The 18-year-old England U19 international joined the League One club in August to gain valuable first-team experience after limited opportunities at the Amex.

Martin has acknowledged Howell’s restricted role, explaining that illness disrupted his early progress. The attacking midfielder initially made a positive impression before a virus affected his fitness and forced the club to manage his minutes carefully.

By the time he returned, Leicester had established a rhythm and altered their formation, leaving Howell struggling to find a suitable place in the side.

In a recent development, there have been encouraging signs when given opportunities, including a league goal and promising contributions from the bench in the FA Cup. However, the overall lack of playing time means the loan has fallen short of its primary objective.

Recent findings suggest that howell was intended to be a key player for Leicester City this season but for a multitude of reasons that has not happened. With that in mind, it is no surprise that Brighton are considering moving him on.

However, that should not be a real issue for LCFC for the rest of the season. The Foxes have plenty of options in that area, with the likes of Kamari Doyle and Sammy Braybrooke currently in fine form.

In a recent development, losing loanee Howell may mean that Leicester can go out and bring in another loanee in January with a squad spot opening up. With players like Conor Chaplin, Tommy Watson and Liam Cullen also in the squad, they can likely afford to bring in a play in another area instead of a direct replacement.

Sublime England thrash Croatia in best performance for a decade
